definition_zh: 金属；金属材料；铁轨；重金属音乐
definition_en: a solid element or material such as iron, copper or gold, usually shiny and able to conduct heat and electricity; also a railway term and a music genre
core_image: 磁铁吊起一堆压扁的铁皮，金属在灯下泛出冷硬的光
scene: 天快黑的废料场里，吊臂上的磁铁把压扁的车壳吸到半空，铁皮互相碰撞发出脆响。A magnet lifted the crushed metal above the scrapyard.
sceneCN: 这里是「金属」（第 1 个义项：有光泽、能导电的元素）；句意为磁铁把压扁的金属吸到废料场上空。图中可辨识物件：磁铁吊臂、压扁的车壳、废料场。

pos.zh: 金属；金属材料；铁轨；重金属音乐

derivatives.zh: 由 metal 加 -ic 构成，义为「金属的；有金属光泽的」
由 metal 词干与希腊语表示「工作」的词组合，义为「冶金学」
由 metal 与 work 复合，义为「金属加工；金属制品」

senses.title: A class of shiny, workable elements
senses.definition: a chemical element such as iron, copper or gold that is usually shiny, conducts heat and electricity, and can be shaped
senses.definitionCN: 铁、铜、金一类通常有光泽、能导热导电、可加工成型的化学元素
senses.example: Iron and copper are the metals most often used in wiring and tools.
senses.exampleCN: 铁和铜是最常用于电线和工具的金属。
senses.why: Greek metallon first named what miners dug out of the earth, so the word began as the stuff of mines rather than as a chemical class; shine and weight were noticed afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 metallon 最初指矿工从地下挖出的东西，所以这个词的起点是「矿井的产出」，而不是化学分类；光泽与重量是后来才被注意到的特征。

senses.title: The material used for making things
senses.definition: the solid material obtained from such elements or their alloys, used to make tools, machines and structures
senses.definitionCN: 由这类元素或其合金得到的固态材料，用来制作工具、机器和建筑结构
senses.example: The old gate is solid metal, so it will not burn.
senses.exampleCN: 这扇旧门是实心金属做的，所以烧不起来。
senses.why: Once metallon named the mined substance, speakers could treat it as a mass that gates and engines are made of, so the word came to name raw material rather than a list of elements.
senses.whyCN: 既然 metallon 指采出的那种物质，说话人就能把它当成造门、造机器的「料」，于是词义落在原料上，而不是一份元素清单。

senses.title: Railway rails, in British usage
senses.definition: the steel rails of a railway line, usually in the plural in British railway talk
senses.definitionCN: 铁路线上的钢轨，通常用复数，是英国铁路行业的说法
senses.example: The signal failed, and the train stopped on the metals.
senses.exampleCN: 信号失灵，列车停在了铁轨上。
senses.why: Rails are the heaviest pieces of metal a passenger ever rides over, so railway talk lets the material stand in for the object made from it.
senses.whyCN: 钢轨是乘客每天压过的最重的金属件，铁路行话便用材料名代替成品，直接把它叫作 metals。

senses.title: Heavy metal music
senses.definition: a loud genre of rock music, short for heavy metal, built on distorted guitars and heavy drumming
senses.definitionCN: 一种喧闹的摇滚乐类型，是 heavy metal 的简称，以失真吉他和沉重鼓点为主
senses.example: He grew up on metal and still keeps the old records.
senses.exampleCN: 他听重金属长大，至今还留着那些旧唱片。
senses.why: The music imitates the weight of dense metal in sound, so the genre borrowed the material name to describe how it feels rather than what it is made of.
senses.whyCN: 这种音乐用声音模仿致密金属的重量感，于是曲风借用材料名来描述听感，而不是描述材质。

intro.en: Metal travelled from a Greek word for a mine through Latin and French before English used it for the shiny substance and then for a music genre.
intro.cn: metal 从一个表示「矿井」的希腊词出发，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，先指那种发亮的物质，后来又指一种音乐类型。

items.en: Metallon covered a mine, the ore dug from it and the metal smelted out of it; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: metallon 兼指矿井、采出的矿石和冶炼出的金属；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as metallum and kept both the mining and the metal senses.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊名词写作 metallum，同时保留采矿与金属两层意思。

items.en: Old French passed metal to English as the name of the substance, stripped of the mine.
items.cn: 古法语把 metal 传给英语，只留下「物质」这一层，矿井的意思脱落了。

items.en: Middle English metal named the substance and also a person's temper, the two uses sharing one spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语的 metal 既指金属，也指人的性情，两种用法共用一个拼写。

items.en: Modern English split the spellings: metal kept the material, mettle kept the courage, and later the word was extended to rails and to heavy music.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写分开：metal 保留材料义，mettle 保留勇气义；后来词义又扩展到铁轨与重金属音乐。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Greek and Latin metal stem; the near-meaning group gathers other words for metals and metal-bearing rock.
note.cn: 形近组收希腊语与拉丁语 metal 词干上的同族词；近义组收其他表示金属与含金属矿石的词。

entries.definition: Made of metal, or bright and hard like it.
entries.definitionCN: 金属制的，或像金属一样光亮坚硬。

entries.definition: The science of getting metal from ore and preparing it for use.
entries.definitionCN: 从矿石中提取金属并加以处理的技术。

entries.definition: Courage and spirit; a doublet whose spelling split off from metal.
entries.definitionCN: 勇气与气概；拼写从 metal 分化出来的同源词。

entries.definition: An element whose properties sit between metals and non-metals.
entries.definitionCN: 性质介于金属与非金属之间的元素。

entries.definition: A hard, heavy metal used for tools and structures.
entries.definitionCN: 一种坚硬沉重的金属，用于工具和建筑。

entries.definition: An alloy of iron and carbon, stronger and harder than iron.
entries.definitionCN: 铁与碳的合金，比铁更硬更强。

entries.definition: A metal made by melting two or more metals together.
entries.definitionCN: 把两种或多种金属熔合而成的金属。

entries.definition: Rock or earth from which metal can be taken.
entries.definitionCN: 可以从中提取金属的矿石或泥土。

normalIntro.en: The word came out of the mine, and its family keeps splitting into material, craft, courage and sound.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自矿井，它的同族一路分到材料、工艺、勇气和声音。

normal.en: Greek metallon named what miners dug out, so metal began as the stuff of mines rather than a chemical category.
normal.cn: 希腊语 metallon 指矿工挖出来的东西，所以 metal 起初是矿井的产出，而不是化学分类。

normal.en: Mettle is the same word with a different spelling: the courage sense kept the old form while metal kept the material sense.
normal.cn: mettle 是同一个词的另一种拼写：勇气义保留了旧形，metal 则保留材料义。

normal.en: Metallic adds -ic, the suffix that turns a noun into the meaning relating to metal.
normal.cn: metallic 加的是 -ic，这个后缀把名词变成「与金属有关的」。

normal.en: Metallurgy joins metal to the Greek word for work, so the name says working metal rather than merely having it.
normal.cn: metallurgy 把 metal 与希腊语中表示「工作」的词结合，名字强调对金属的加工，而不是拥有金属。

normal.en: Heavy metal takes the weight of the material into music, which is why the genre is described as dense and loud.
normal.cn: heavy metal 把材料的重量带进音乐，所以这种曲风被形容为致密、喧闹。

abstract.en: Picture a mine, a furnace and a rail: one substance travelling from rock to engine.
abstract.cn: 想象矿井、熔炉和铁轨：同一种物质从岩石一路走到发动机上。

abstract.en: A word for a chemical element can also name a music genre, which shows how far a material word can drift into sound.
abstract.cn: 一个表示化学元素的词也能指一种音乐类型，可见材料词能漂移到多远的声音领域。

abstract.en: Every trusted tool is a lump of metal someone shaped, and the word still carries that dependence.
abstract.cn: 每件可信赖的工具都曾是某人塑形的一块金属，这个词仍带着这份依赖。

examples.en: The magnet lifted the crushed metal out of the pile.
examples.cn: 磁铁把压扁的金属从废料堆里吸了出来。

examples.en: Copper is a metal that carries electricity well.
examples.cn: 铜是一种导电性很好的金属。

examples.en: The band plays metal every Friday night.
examples.cn: 这支乐队每周五夜里都演奏重金属。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖铁」——收废品的人一喊卖铁，卖的就是一堆金属；记住 metal 是金属。

root: 希腊语 metallon（矿井、金属）经拉丁语 metallum 与古法语 metal 进入英语；同族词多与金属、冶金有关，另有拼写分化的 mettle 表示勇气。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the mined substance; from it the senses run to the material, to the rails made of it, and finally to a music named after its weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是矿井里采出的那种物质；义项由此走向材料、走向用材料铺成的铁轨，最后走向以它的重量命名的音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnet lifting crushed steel, the metal cold and bright under the yard lights.
core.cn: 核心意象：磁铁吊起压扁的钢壳，金属在废料场的灯下又冷又亮。

branches.en: a magnet lifting crushed cars in a scrapyard
branches.cn: 废料场上磁铁吊起压扁的车壳

branches.en: a steel girder holding up a motorway
branches.cn: 撑起高速公路的钢梁

branches.en: a train waiting on the rails at a red signal
branches.cn: 红灯前停在铁轨上的列车

branches.en: a wall of speakers at a loud concert
branches.cn: 喧闹演出里的一整面音箱墙

branches.en: one substance running from the mine to the machine
branches.cn: 同一种物质从矿井一路走到机器上

intro.en: The word rests on a Greek mine-word and its Latin borrowing, with two English suffixes and a compound that carry the family outward.
intro.cn: 这个词立在希腊语表示矿井的词及其拉丁借词上，再由两个英语后缀和一个复合词把词族向外撑开。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 方法；办法；条理；体系；（学科或艺术的）方法论体系
definition_en: a particular way of doing something, especially one that is planned and systematic, or the order and system that such a way produces
core_image: 一条被反复踩出的小路：草被踩平了，路指向远处的目标
scene: 老实验室里的那套流程几十年没有变过。The lab still uses a method that has not changed in forty years.
sceneCN: 这里 method 是「方法」（第 1 个义项：做某事的特定程序）；句意：这个实验室仍在使用一套四十年没变过的方法。场景要点：一排贴着编号的旧仪器、墙上手写的步骤表、被踩得发亮的地面；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.phrase: there is method in one's madness

derivatives.zh: 有条理的；按部就班的
有条理地；系统地
方法论；一套研究方法

senses.title: A way of doing something
senses.titleCN: 方法：做某事的特定路数
senses.definition: a particular procedure for doing something, especially a planned and systematic one
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的特定程序，尤指有计划、有系统的程序
senses.example: The lab still uses a method that has not changed in forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验室仍在使用一套四十年没变过的方法。
senses.why: Method reached English in the early 15th century from Greek methodos, originally 'pursuit, a following after'. A method is a path that has already been walked and can be walked again.
senses.whyCN: method 于 15 世纪初从希腊语 methodos 进入英语，原义为“追寻、跟随其后”。方法就是一条已经被人走过、还可以再走一遍的路。

senses.title: Orderliness
senses.definition: the quality of acting in an orderly, systematic way rather than at random
senses.definitionCN: 做事有条理、有系统，而非随意的品质
senses.example: There was method in the way she sorted the files, though no one else could see it.
senses.exampleCN: 她整理文件的方式自有章法，只是别人看不出来。
senses.why: From the 1610s the word also named 'orderliness, regularity'. The path is no longer a particular route but the habit of always walking on one.
senses.whyCN: 自 17 世纪 10 年代起，这个词也指“有条理、有规律”。此时路不再是一条具体路线，而是“总要沿着某条路走”的习惯。

senses.title: A complete system
senses.definition: a complete set of rules or procedures for attaining an end
senses.definitionCN: 为达到某一目的而设的一整套规则或程序
senses.example: The school adopted a new method for teaching reading.
senses.exampleCN: 学校采用了一套新的阅读教学体系。
senses.why: The sense 'a system or complete set of rules' is recorded from the 1680s. Once a path is written down as rules, it can be taught to strangers.
senses.whyCN: “体系或完整规则集”这一义项自 17 世纪 80 年代有记录。一旦一条路被写成规则，它就能教给陌生人。

senses.title: Scientific method
senses.titleCN: 科学方法：学科自己的路
senses.definition: the established procedure of a discipline for testing claims and producing knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科为检验主张、生产知识而确立的程序
senses.example: The scientific method is less a single recipe than a set of habits of doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 科学方法与其说是一份单一配方，不如说是一组怀疑的习惯。
senses.why: Greek methodos already meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry'. Science did not invent the word; it inherited the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 methodos 本就意为“科学探究、探究的方法”。科学没有发明这个词，它继承的是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Teaching and acting methods
senses.titleCN: 教学法与表演体系：一门手艺的路
senses.definition: a named system of practice in teaching or in the arts, such as the direct method or method acting
senses.definitionCN: 教学或艺术中以人名或特征命名的实践体系，如直接教学法、方法派表演
senses.example: Method acting asks the performer to draw on real memories.
senses.exampleCN: 方法派表演要求演员调动真实的记忆。
senses.why: A system with a name becomes a school. Method here is a path that a whole profession agrees to walk together.
senses.whyCN: 一套有名字的体系会变成一派。这里的 method 是一整门行业同意一起走的那条路。

senses.title: Old medical sense
senses.titleCN: 医学旧义：系统化的治疗方案
senses.definition: in early use, the regular, systematic treatment of disease
senses.definitionCN: 在早期用法中，指对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗
senses.example: The medieval physician spoke of a method for fevers, not a single remedy.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的医生讲的是治疗热病的一套方法，而不是某一味药。
senses.why: The first English sense, in the early 15th century, was 'regular, systematic treatment of disease'. The word entered through medicine before it belonged to everything else.
senses.whyCN: 英语中的第一个义项是 15 世纪初的“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”。这个词先通过医学进来，然后才属于一切别的事物。

senses.title: Method in programming
senses.titleCN: 编程中的方法：对象身上的函数
senses.definition: in object-oriented programming, a function or procedure attached to an object or class
senses.definitionCN: 在面向对象编程中，附着于对象或类上的函数或过程
senses.example: The method returns a new list instead of changing the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法返回一个新列表，而不修改旧列表。
senses.why: The metaphor survives in code: a method is still a fixed route the object knows how to take when it is called.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻在代码里活了下来：方法仍是对象被调用时知道该怎么走的一条固定路线。

senses.title: A method of inquiry
senses.titleCN: 探究之路：哲学意义上的方法
senses.definition: in philosophy, the deliberate path of doubt or reasoning by which a conclusion is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中，为抵达结论而有意采取的怀疑或推理之路
senses.example: Descartes began with a method of doubt that would leave only certainty standing.
senses.exampleCN: 笛卡尔从一种怀疑的方法开始，只为留下确定的东西。
senses.why: Methodos was literally a following after something. Philosophy turns that pursuit into a rule for how to pursue anything at all.
senses.whyCN: methodos 字面上就是“跟在某物之后追”。哲学把这趟追寻变成一条规则，规定该怎样追寻任何东西。

senses.title: Method in one's madness
senses.definition: in the phrase 'there is method in one's madness', used when apparently foolish behaviour turns out to have a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 「there is method in one's madness」 中，指看似荒唐的行为其实自有目的
senses.example: He shuffles the cards for ten minutes, but there is method in his madness.
senses.exampleCN: 他把牌洗了十分钟，看似荒唐，其实自有章法。
senses.why: Shakespeare's phrase 'though this be madness, yet there is method in it' (Hamlet) gave English a fixed way to say that a path is hidden inside chaos.
senses.whyCN: 莎士比亚的句子“though this be madness, yet there is method in it”（《哈姆雷特》）给了英语一个固定说法：混乱里藏着一条路。

intro.en: Method is Greek: meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road, way'. Latin borrowed it as methodus and passed it to French and English. It has no connection with medical, despite the shared -met- shape. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: method 是希腊词：meta“追寻”加 hodos“路、道”。拉丁语把它借作 methodus，再传给法语和英语。尽管有共同的 -met- 外形，它与 medical 毫无关系。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'regular, systematic treatment of disease', through Latin methodus 'way of teaching or going' and Greek methodos.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 15 世纪初，意为“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”，经拉丁语 methodus“教学或行走之道”与希腊语 methodos 而来。

items.en: Greek methodos meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry, investigation', and originally 'pursuit, a following after'.
items.cn: 希腊语 methodos 意为“科学探究、探究的方法、调查”，原义为“追寻、跟随其后”。

items.en: The word joins meta 'in pursuit or quest of' and hodos 'a way, path, track, road', also 'a journey'. Hodos is of uncertain origin; Beekes suggests PIE *sod- 'course', and it is traditionally linked to Slavic words for 'course'.
items.cn: 这个词由 meta“追寻、求索”与 hodos“路、路径、轨道、道路”（也指“旅程”）组合而成。hodos 的来源不确定；Beekes 提出原始印欧语 *sod-“行程”，传统上也把它与斯拉夫语表示“行程”的词联系起来。

items.en: The sense widened to 'any way of doing anything' in the 1580s, to 'orderliness, regularity' in the 1610s, and to 'a system or complete set of rules' in the 1680s.
items.cn: 词义在 16 世纪 80 年代扩展到“做任何事的方式”，17 世纪 10 年代扩展到“有条理、有规律”，17 世纪 80 年代扩展到“体系或完整的一套规则”。

items.en: The phrase method acting is recorded in reference to the theory associated with the Russian director Konstantin Stanislavski.
items.cn: method acting 这一说法有记录，指与俄国导演康斯坦丁·斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基相关的理论。

items.en: Medical goes back to Latin medicus 'physician', with no Greek element. Meta- in method is the Greek preposition 'in pursuit of', not the modern prefix meaning 'beyond' or 'after'; the two words only share letters.
items.cn: medical 追溯到拉丁语 medicus“医生”，不含希腊语成分。method 里的 meta- 是希腊语介词“追寻”，不是现代表示“超越、之后”的前缀；两个词只共享字母。

note.en: The first group is the word family built on method: the adjective, the adverb and the study of method. The second group compares the nouns English uses for 'a way of doing something', which differ in scale and in who owns the way.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 method 上的词族：形容词、副词与研究方法的学问。第二组比较英语里表示“做某事的方式”的几个名词，区别在于尺度大小与“这条路归谁”。

entries.definition: the branch of knowledge that studies methods, or the set of methods used in a field. It is not a longer synonym of method: a methodology can contain several methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究方法的学问分支，或某一领域所使用的一套方法。它不是 method 的加长同义词：一套方法论里可以包含好几种方法。

entries.definition: done according to a method; orderly and systematic. It describes a person or a procedure, not a route.
entries.definitionCN: 按方法进行的；有条理、有系统的。它描述人或程序，而不描述一条路线。

entries.definition: in an orderly, step-by-step way. It answers 'how', while method answers 'by what route'.
entries.definitionCN: 有条理地、一步一步地。它回答“怎样做”，而 method 回答“走哪条路”。

entries.definition: to reduce something to order or system. The verb turns the noun into an action; it is rare outside formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物整理成秩序或体系。这个动词把名词变成动作；在正式写作之外很少见。

entries.definition: a way of dealing with a problem or subject, often including the attitude behind it. It is broader and softer than method, which implies explicit steps.
entries.definitionCN: 处理问题或课题的方式，常包含背后的态度。它比 method 更宽、更软，而 method 暗示明确的步骤。

entries.definition: a particular way of carrying out a single task, especially one requiring skill. Techniques are the small parts inside a method.
entries.definitionCN: 完成单项任务的具体方式，尤指需要技巧的那种。technique 是 method 内部的一个个小零件。

entries.definition: a thing or resource used to achieve an end. Means answers 'with what'; method answers 'in what order'.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目的而使用的东西或资源。means 回答“用什么”，method 回答“按什么顺序”。

entries.definition: an established or official sequence of steps. It is more bureaucratic than method and often written down by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 既定的或官方的步骤顺序。它比 method 更带行政色彩，常由某个权威写下来。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road', the Latin borrowing methodus, and the family methodical, methodology, methodize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”、拉丁语借词 methodus，以及 methodical、methodology、methodize 词族。

normal.en: hodos means 'road'. A method is literally 'a following after on a road': meta plus hodos.
normal.cn: hodos 意为“路”。method 字面上就是“沿路跟随”：meta 加 hodos。

normal.en: In method, meta- does not mean 'beyond' or 'after' as it does in modern English; it means 'in pursuit of'. The Greek preposition is about chasing, not about position.
normal.cn: 在 method 里，meta- 不像现代英语那样表示“超越”或“之后”，而是“追寻”。这个希腊语介词讲的是追赶，不是位置。

normal.en: Methodology is not a fancy word for method: it is the study of methods, or the whole set of them used in a field.
normal.cn: methodology 不是 method 的高级说法：它是对方法的研究，或某一领域所使用的整套方法。

normal.en: Methodical describes the person who always walks on a path; method names the path itself.
normal.cn: methodical 描述那个总沿着路走的人；method 命名的是那条路本身。

normal.en: Medical looks similar but is Latin medicus 'physician'. One word has a road in it, the other has a doctor.
normal.cn: medical 看着像，其实是拉丁语 medicus“医生”。一个词里装着一条路，另一个词里装着一位医生。

abstract.en: Picture grass in a field. One path is visible because many feet chose the same line; that line is a method.
abstract.cn: 想象一片草地。有一条路看得见，是因为许多脚选择了同一条线；那条线就是 method。

abstract.en: A path can be walked by one person or written down for a school. The moment it is written down, method becomes methodology.
abstract.cn: 一条路可以由一个人走，也可以写下来给一个学派。写下来的那一刻，method 就变成了 methodology。

abstract.en: Method is the order of steps, not the tool in your hand. A hammer is a means; how you swing it is a technique; the sequence is the method.
abstract.cn: method 是步骤的顺序，不是你手里的工具。锤子是 means；怎么挥是 technique；先后次序才是 method。

examples.en: No method will save a study that was badly designed in the first place.
examples.cn: 如果一项研究一开始就设计得很糟，任何方法都救不了它。

examples.en: She works without method, yet somehow finishes before everyone else.
examples.cn: 她做事毫无章法，却总能比别人先做完。

examples.en: The two laboratories use different methods and keep getting different numbers.
examples.cn: 两个实验室用不同的方法，得到的数字也一直不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: “卖瑟德”——卖瑟德把一条踩出来的小路画在纸上，卖给后来的人照着走 → method 方法、办法（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自希腊语 methodos“追寻、探究”，由 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”构成，核心是“沿着一条路追到目标”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of method, all from one image: a line worn into the grass by feet that wanted the same destination. It can be one path, the habit of taking paths, or the written map of them.
sensesIntro.cn: method 的九个义项都来自同一幅画面：一条被想抵达同一目标的脚踩出来的草径。它可以是某一条路、走路的习惯，或被写下来的路线图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path worn into grass, pointing at a destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被踩进草地的小路，指向某个目的地。

branches.en: THE PATH: the oldest senses name a procedure, first for curing disease, then for anything at all.
branches.cn: 路：最老的义项命名一套程序，先用于治病，后用于任何事。

branches.en: THE HABIT: orderliness is walking on a path by choice, and the idiom says a path may hide inside apparent chaos.
branches.cn: 习惯：条理是有意识地沿路走；那条习语则说，混乱里也可能藏着一条路。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: written rules turn a path into a teachable system, and science inherits the oldest 'inquiry' sense.
branches.cn: 体系：写下来的规则把路变成可教的体系，而科学继承的是最古老的“探究”义。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: teaching and acting give the path a proper name, and philosophy makes the pursuit itself a rule.
branches.cn: 学派：教学与表演给这条路一个专名，哲学则把追寻本身变成规则。

branches.en: THE CODE: in software the object still knows a fixed route to take when called.
branches.cn: 代码：在软件里，对象被调用时仍知道该走哪条固定路线。

intro.en: Method is a Greek compound borrowed whole: meta- plus hodos 'road'. English adds -ical, -ically, -ology, -ologist and -ize, while the same hodos builds episode, period and Exodus.
intro.cn: method 是整体借入的希腊语复合词：meta- 加 hodos“路”。英语加上 -ical、-ically、-ology、-ologist、-ize，而同一个 hodos 还构成 episode、period、Exodus。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek word unchanged as methodus 'way of teaching or going', and Late Latin methodicus came from Greek methodikos. Latin had its own word for 'way', modus, but method did not come from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语原样吸收希腊词作 methodus“教学或行走之道”，晚期拉丁语 methodicus 来自希腊语 methodikos。拉丁语自己表示“方式”的词是 modus，但 method 并非来自它。

items.meaning: a following after on a road; a way of doing something
items.meaningCN: 沿路追寻；做某事的方法（meta- 追寻 + hodos 路）
items.example: They tried every method and failed with each.
items.exampleCN: 他们试了每一种方法，每一种都失败了。

items.meaningCN: 按方法进行的；有条理的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: His methodical notes filled four notebooks.
items.exampleCN: 他条理分明的笔记写满了四个本子。

items.meaningCN: 有条理地；一步一步地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 她逐个抽屉有条理地检查。

items.meaning: the study of methods; a set of methods used in a field
items.meaningCN: 方法论；一套研究方法（-ology 表学问）
items.example: The paper was rejected for its weak methodology.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文因方法论薄弱而被拒。

items.example: The two studies differ on methodological grounds.
items.exampleCN: 这两项研究在方法上存在分歧。

items.meaning: a specialist in methods of research
items.example: A methodologist was added to the review panel.
items.exampleCN: 评审组里增加了一位方法论专家。

items.meaning: to arrange according to a system
items.meaningCN: 使有条理；使系统化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: He methodized the archive over one winter.
items.exampleCN: 他用一个冬天把档案整理成体系。

items.meaning: a member of the Protestant denomination founded at Oxford in 1729
items.meaningCN: 卫理公会教徒（-ist 表追随者，源于其讲究方法的修行方式）
items.example: The Methodist chapel still stands on the corner.
items.exampleCN: 卫理公会礼拜堂仍立在街角。

items.structure: epi- (besides) + eisodos (a coming in, from hodos 'way')
items.meaning: an incident or instalment inserted into a larger whole
items.meaningCN: 插曲；（系列中的）一集（epi- 另外 + eisodos 进入，含 hodos 路）
items.exampleCN: 最后一集什么也没解答。

items.meaning: a going round; a length of time
items.meaningCN: 周期；一段时间（peri- 环绕 + hodos 路，即“绕一圈”）
items.example: The period lasted almost a century.
items.exampleCN: 这一时期持续了将近一个世纪。

items.meaning: a going out; a mass departure
items.meaningCN: 出走；大批离去（ex- 向外 + hodos 路）
items.example: The drought set off an exodus from the villages.
items.exampleCN: 旱灾引发了村庄的大批出走。

items.meaning: a performance technique that draws on the actor's own experience
items.meaningCN: 方法派表演（以体系命名的表演技术）
items.example: Method acting changed how American films were shot.
items.exampleCN: 方法派表演改变了美国电影的拍摄方式。

definition_zh: 公制的；度量的；格律的；度量指标
definition_en: based on the metric system; also relating to measurement or to poetic metre, and as a noun a measure used to judge performance
core_image: 一把带刻度的尺，把长度拆成一个个可以比较的数字
scene: 实验室的白板上列着两套单位，年轻的研究员把英制数字逐个换算成公制。The intern turned every figure on the board into metric units.
sceneCN: 这里是「公制的」（第 1 个义项：使用公制单位计量）；句意为实习生把白板上的每个数字都换成了公制单位。图中可辨识物件：白板、粉笔、写满数字的表格。

derivatives.zh: 由 metric 加 -al 构成，义为「格律的；度量的」
由 metric 加 -ation 构成，义为「改用公制」
由 metrical 加 -ly 构成，义为「按公制地；按格律地」

senses.title: Relating to the metric system
senses.definition: using or based on the metric system, in which units such as the metre and the kilogram are used
senses.definitionCN: 使用或基于公制的，即以米、千克等单位计量
senses.example: The label lists the weight in metric units.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上用公制单位标注重量。
senses.why: The Greek root metron meant a measure, and after the French reform the adjective was attached to the system built on the metre, so metric labels anything counted in those units.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 metron 意为「尺度」，法国公制改革之后这个形容词被贴到以米为基础的那套单位上，凡是按这套单位计量的东西都叫 metric。

senses.title: A measurement used to judge performance
senses.definition: a measurement used to judge performance or progress, most often in the plural form metrics
senses.definitionCN: 用来衡量表现或进展的测量值，最常用复数形式 metrics
senses.example: The team reviews three metrics every Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每周一复盘三项指标。
senses.why: If metron is any measure, then a single number taken from a process is also a metron, and business English turned that into the countable metrics of a dashboard.
senses.whyCN: 既然 metron 泛指任何一种度量，那么从流程里取出一个数字也是一种度量，商业英语便把它变成仪表盘上可数的 metrics。

senses.title: Of measurement in general
senses.definition: concerned with measuring distance, size or quantity rather than with the units of one particular system
senses.definitionCN: 与距离、大小或数量的测量有关，而不是特指某一套单位
senses.example: In a metric space, distance is defined by a rule rather than by a ruler.
senses.exampleCN: 在度量空间里，距离由一条规则定义，而不是用尺子量出。
senses.why: Mathematics kept the oldest sense of metron as sheer measure, so metric can describe any structure that allows a distance to be assigned, with no metres or inches involved.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留了 metron 最古老的「度量」本义，因此 metric 可以描述任何一种能给出距离的结构，与米或英寸都无关。

senses.title: Of poetic metre
senses.definition: relating to metre, the patterned rhythm of stressed and unstressed syllables in verse
senses.definitionCN: 与格律有关的，即诗句中轻重音节形成的节奏模式
senses.example: The critic counted the metric feet in each line.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者数了每一行里的格律音步。
senses.why: Greek metrikos described verse measured out in feet, and the same adjective survived in literary criticism long after it had been applied to weights and lengths.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 metrikos 本指按音步「量」出来的诗句，这个形容词在文学批评里一直保留，后来才被用到重量与长度上。

intro.en: Metric comes from a Greek word for measure, reached English through Latin and French, and split between the sense of a system of units and the sense of a numbered measure.
intro.cn: metric 出自希腊语中表示「度量」的词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，并在「单位体系」与「可计量的数值」两个方向上都站稳了脚。

items.en: Metron was any measure or unit of length, and it also named the unit of rhythm in verse.
items.cn: metron 泛指任何尺度或长度单位，也指诗句中节奏的单位。

items.en: The adjective metrikos meant of measure and was used especially for the measured rhythm of poetry.
items.cn: 形容词 metrikos 意为「关于度量的」，尤用于诗句中被量出的节奏。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as metricus, keeping the literary and measuring senses together.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词写作 metricus，把文学与度量两层意思一并保留。

items.en: During the French reform of weights and measures, the word was fixed to the system based on the metre, and the phrase système métrique spread across Europe.
items.cn: 在法国度量衡改革中，这个词被固定到以米为基础的体系上，système métrique 这一说法传遍欧洲。

items.en: English took metric in the nineteenth century for the system of units, then reused it for any number a business tracks and for the older sense of verse rhythm.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入 metric 指单位体系，随后又用它指企业追踪的任何数值，并保留了诗律的旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek measure root through metre, geometry and the derived adjective; the near-meaning group collects words for measuring and for standards of comparison.
note.cn: 形近组顺着希腊语「度量」词根，收 metre、geometry 与派生形容词；近义组收表示测量与比较标准的词。

entries.definition: The base unit of length in the metric system.
entries.definitionCN: 公制中长度的基本单位。

entries.definition: The American spelling of metre; also a device that measures.
entries.definitionCN: metre 的美式拼写；也指计量仪表。

entries.definition: Relating to poetic metre or to measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 与诗律或度量有关的。

entries.definition: The mathematics of shapes and distances, named from measuring the earth.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形状与距离的数学，名字来自「测量土地」。

entries.definition: The act or result of finding a size or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 测量行为或测量所得的结果。

entries.definition: A fixed amount used as a standard for measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 作为计量标准的固定量。

entries.definition: An instrument or standard used for measuring something.
entries.definitionCN: 测量用的仪器或标准。

entries.definition: A standard point of reference for judging performance.
entries.definitionCN: 评判表现所用的参照标准。

normalIntro.en: One Greek word for measure runs through units, geometry and verse, so the family looks scattered but keeps a single idea.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「度量」的希腊词贯穿单位、几何与诗句，所以这一族看着分散，内核却只有一个。

normal.en: Metron is Greek for a measure, and metre is the measure the metric system starts from.
normal.cn: metron 是希腊语中的「尺度」，metre 正是公制起步的那把尺。

normal.en: Metric as an adjective belongs to the system, which is why metric system and metric unit appear as fixed pairs.
normal.cn: 作形容词的 metric 依附于这套体系，所以 metric system 与 metric unit 是固定搭配。

normal.en: Metrics, the plural noun, turns one measurement into the set of numbers a dashboard watches.
normal.cn: 复数名词 metrics 把一次测量变成仪表盘上盯着的一组数字。

normal.en: Geometry ends in the same Greek word, so its name literally means measuring the land.
normal.cn: geometry 的词尾是同一个希腊词，名字字面上就是「测量土地」。

normal.en: Metrical keeps the verse sense, because Greek metre also counted the feet of a line.
normal.cn: metrical 保留了诗句的义项，因为希腊语的 metre 也用来数一行诗的音步。

abstract.en: A ruler and a dashboard do the same thing: they turn the world into numbers someone can compare.
abstract.cn: 尺子和仪表盘做的是同一件事：把世界变成可以互相比较的数字。

abstract.en: The word sits between a poem and a machine, measuring both a line of verse and a sack of grain.
abstract.cn: 这个词站在诗与机器之间，既量一行诗，也称一袋粮食。

abstract.en: Choosing what to count is choosing what matters, so a metric is never a neutral number.
abstract.cn: 决定数什么，就是决定在意什么，所以指标从来不是中立的数字。

examples.en: The form asks for your height in metric units.
examples.cn: 表格要求用公制单位填写身高。

examples.en: We track two metrics: response time and error rate.
examples.cn: 我们跟踪两项指标：响应时间和错误率。

examples.en: The poet kept a strict metric pattern in every line.
examples.cn: 这位诗人在每一行都保持严格的格律。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米特里克」——头一个字就是米，公制从米量起；记住 metric 是公制的，也指度量指标。

root: 希腊语 metron（尺度）派生 metrikos（关于度量的），经晚期拉丁语 metricus 与法语 métrique 进入英语；同族词包括 metre 与 geometry。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of measuring; the senses divide into a system of units, a countable number on a dashboard, measurement in general, and the measured rhythm of verse.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「度量」这个动作；义项分到单位体系、仪表盘上的可数数值、一般意义的测量，以及被量出节奏的诗句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler with fine marks, turning length into numbers that can be compared.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刻着细密刻度的尺，把长度变成可以互相比较的数字。

branches.en: a cookbook printing grams beside ounces
branches.cn: 食谱上把克与盎司并排印出

branches.en: a dashboard with three numbers on it
branches.cn: 仪表盘上只挂着三个数字

branches.en: a map where distance comes from a rule, not a ruler
branches.cn: 地图上的距离由规则给出，而不是用尺量

branches.en: a line of verse scanned for its beat
branches.cn: 一行诗被数出它的节拍

branches.en: the same act of measuring, once in units and once in numbers
branches.cn: 同一个测量动作，一次落在单位上，一次落在数字上

intro.en: Greek measure and its adjective supply the stem, and English suffixes and the geometry compound carry the family in several directions.
intro.cn: 希腊语的「度量」名词与形容词提供词干，再由英语后缀与 geometry 这个复合词把词族引向几个方向。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 麦克风；传声器；话筒；窃听器
definition_en: a device that picks up sound and turns it into an electrical signal, especially the part a performer speaks into or a small hidden pickup
core_image: 一根细长的杆，把说话声收进一道看不见的电信号
scene: 演播室里，主持人把支架拉近，确认声音能送到最后一排观众的耳朵。The host leaned toward the microphone and opened the show.
sceneCN: 这里是「话筒」（第 2 个义项：供人对着说话的部件）；句意为主持人俯身靠近话筒开始节目。图中可辨识物件：话筒架、演播台、指示灯。

pos.zh: 麦克风；传声器；话筒；窃听器

derivatives.zh: 由 microphone 缩略而来，口语中读作单音节，义为「麦克风」
由 microphone 加 -ic 构成，义为「微音效应的；拾音引起的」
由 microphone 加 -y 构成，义为「微音效应」

senses.title: A device that turns sound into a signal
senses.definition: an instrument that picks up sound waves and converts them into an electrical signal
senses.definitionCN: 拾取声波并把它转换成电信号的器件
senses.example: A microphone on the table picked up every word of the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上的传声器把会议的每句话都收了进去。
senses.why: The Greek pieces say small sound, and early devices were built to make faint sounds audible, so the name describes catching sound rather than producing it.
senses.whyCN: 两个希腊词素说的是「微小的声音」，早期装置正是为了让微弱的声音能被听见，所以名字描述的是捕捉声音，而非发出声音。

senses.title: The part a performer speaks into
senses.definition: the part of a sound system, headset or instrument that a person speaks or sings directly into
senses.definitionCN: 音响、耳机或乐器上供人直接对着说话或演唱的部件
senses.example: She held the microphone close and lowered her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她把话筒拿近，压低声音唱。
senses.why: Once the signal device is placed in front of a performer, the word stops naming the circuit and starts naming the object aimed at the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 当这种转换器件被摆到表演者嘴前，词义就不再指电路，而开始指那个对准嘴巴的物件。

senses.title: A hidden listening device
senses.definition: a small hidden device that picks up speech so that someone can listen without being seen
senses.definitionCN: 暗藏的小型拾音装置，使人在不被看见的情况下听到谈话
senses.example: They found a microphone under the desk in the empty office.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在空办公室的书桌下面发现了一个窃听器。
senses.why: A device built to catch tiny sounds is exactly what surveillance needs, so the technical name quietly took on the meaning of a bug hidden in a room.
senses.whyCN: 能捕捉细微声响的器件正是监听所需，于是这个技术名称自然而然地多了「藏在房间里的窃听器」这层意思。

intro.en: Microphone is a nineteenth-century coinage from two Greek words, small and voice, and its use moved from faint-sound devices to the electric pickup everyone knows.
intro.cn: microphone 是十九世纪用两个希腊词「小」与「声音」拼成的新词，用法从放大微弱声音的装置转到了人人熟悉的电声拾音器。

items.en: Mikros meant small or little, and it became the first element of many scientific words.
items.cn: mikros 意为小的、细微的，后来成为许多科学词汇的第一个词素。

items.en: Phone meant voice or sound, and it named both the human voice and the sound itself.
items.cn: phone 意为嗓音或声音，既指人的说话声，也指声音本身。

items.en: Writers of scientific Latin and English joined the two elements to name devices for making weak sounds easier to hear; the exact first coining is not settled.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语与英语的作者把两个词素拼起来，命名让微弱声音更容易被听见的装置；具体首见年份尚无定论。

items.en: With carbon transmitters and early telephony, the word settled on the device that converts sound into an electric current.
items.cn: 随着碳粒送话器和早期电话技术，这个词固定指把声音转换成电流的器件。

items.en: Modern English keeps the technical sense and extends it to the pickup on a headset and to a hidden listening bug.
items.cn: 现代英语保留技术义，并把它扩展到耳机上的拾音件和暗藏的窃听装置。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek voice element through short forms and compounds; the near-meaning group collects the other pieces of a sound chain.
note.cn: 形近组顺着希腊语「声音」词素，收简称与复合词；近义组收一条声音链路里的其他器件。

entries.definition: The short spoken form of microphone.
entries.definitionCN: microphone 的口语简称。

entries.definition: A device for speaking to someone at a distance; it shares the voice element.
entries.definitionCN: 远距离通话的装置，与 microphone 共用表示「声音」的词素。

entries.definition: A cone that makes a voice carry much farther.
entries.definitionCN: 把声音传得更远的锥形扩音器。

entries.definition: One of the distinct speech sounds of a language.
entries.definitionCN: 一种语言中彼此区别的语音单位。

entries.definition: A device that turns an electric signal back into sound.
entries.definitionCN: 把电信号还原成声音的装置。

entries.definition: A device that makes a signal stronger before it is sent on.
entries.definitionCN: 在信号送出前把它增强的装置。

entries.definition: A pair of earpieces with a pickup, worn on the head.
entries.definitionCN: 带拾音件的头戴式耳机。

entries.definition: The small part of a device that sits close to the ear.
entries.definitionCN: 设备上贴近耳朵的小部件。

normalIntro.en: Two Greek pieces, small and voice, were joined in the nineteenth century to name a device that catches sound.
normalIntro.cn: 两个希腊词素「小」与「声音」在十九世纪拼在一起，用来命名一种捕捉声音的器件。

normal.en: Micro- means small and -phone means voice, so the compound says small voice before it says anything technical.
normal.cn: micro- 意为「小」，-phone 意为「声音」，所以这个复合词先说的是「小声音」，然后才谈技术。

normal.en: Telephone and megaphone share the same voice element, one for distance and one for reach of volume.
normal.cn: telephone 与 megaphone 共用同一个「声音」词素，一个指距离，一个指音量传得远。

normal.en: Phoneme, phonetics and symphony all descend from the Greek word for voice.
normal.cn: phoneme、phonetics 与 symphony 都出自希腊语中表示「声音」的词。

normal.en: Audio workers write mic, not mike, for the short form, and the spelling marks the trade.
normal.cn: 音频行业把简称写作 mic 而不是 mike，这个拼写本身就是行内标记。

normal.en: A microphone converts rather than creates: the sound must exist before the device can turn it into a signal.
normal.cn: 麦克风只是转换，并不创造：声音必须先存在，器件才能把它变成信号。

abstract.en: A small voice made wide enough to fill a hall.
abstract.cn: 一个很小的声音被放大到能填满整个大厅。

abstract.en: The same pickup can serve a singer and a spy; the tool leaves the purpose to the hand that places it.
abstract.cn: 同一个拾音器可以服务歌手，也可以服务间谍；工具把用途留给摆放它的那只手。

abstract.en: Sound has no shape, yet a microphone gives it something a wire can carry.
abstract.cn: 声音本没有形状，麦克风却给了它一样能被导线带走的东西。

examples.en: She checked the microphone before the interview.
examples.cn: 采访前她检查了话筒。

examples.en: The microphone hidden in the lamp had been there for weeks.
examples.cn: 藏在台灯里的窃听器已经在那里放了好几周。

examples.en: The microphone on the stand was too far from the singer.
examples.cn: 支架上的话筒离歌手太远了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克风」——中文直接音译，麦克风就是 microphone 的常用叫法。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小）与 phone（声音）拼接而成，十九世纪出现，指把声音拾取并转换为电信号的器件；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the conversion of sound into a signal; the senses divide into the pickup, the object a performer faces, and the same device used in secret.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把声音变成信号；义项分到拾音器件、表演者面对的那件物品，以及同一类器件的暗中用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin rod standing in front of a speaker, catching every word into an invisible wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细杆立在说话人面前，把每句话收进一根看不见的线。

branches.en: a faint voice made visible on a screen
branches.cn: 微弱的声音在屏幕上显成一道波形

branches.en: a singer leaning into a stand
branches.cn: 歌手俯身靠近支架

branches.en: a tiny device under a desk
branches.cn: 书桌底下的小装置

branches.en: sound caught first as a signal and then as a performance
branches.cn: 声音先被当作信号收下，再被当作表演送出

branches.en: the same pickup used openly and in secret
branches.cn: 同一个拾音器，一明一暗地用着

intro.en: A Greek prefix for small and a Greek combining form for voice sit on either side of the word, and later English shortenings and compounds extend the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「小」的希腊前缀与一个表示「声音」的希腊构词成分夹住这个词，后来的英语简称与复合词又把词族向外延伸。

latinIntro.en: The word was assembled from Greek elements in the nineteenth century, so no classical Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是十九世纪用希腊词素拼出来的，古典拉丁语中没有它的同族词记录。

items.meaning: device for sound at a distance
device that makes a voice carry

definition_zh: 显微镜；高倍显微设备；严密审视
definition_en: an instrument that makes very small objects look large enough to examine; also any high-power instrument of this kind and a figurative state of close scrutiny
core_image: 一枚镜片把叶片上的小格子放大到眼前
scene: 实验台上摆着切片和光源，学生们轮流俯身看那片薄薄的叶片。Through the microscope, the leaf showed rows of tiny green cells.
sceneCN: 这里是「显微镜」（第 1 个义项：放大微小物体的仪器）；句意为透过显微镜，叶片显出成排的绿色小细胞。图中可辨识物件：显微镜、载玻片、叶片。

pos.zh: 显微镜；高倍显微设备；严密审视

collocations.zh: 在显微镜下；受到严密审视

derivatives.zh: 由 microscope 词干加 -ic 构成，义为「显微镜的；小到看不见的」
由 microscope 词干加 -y 构成，义为「显微镜术；显微检查」
由 microscope 加 -ist 构成，义为「显微镜使用者；显微镜专家」

senses.title: An instrument that magnifies small things
senses.definition: a scientific instrument with lenses that makes very small objects look large enough to examine
senses.definitionCN: 装有透镜、能把极小的物体放大到足以观察的科学仪器
senses.example: Under the microscope, the onion skin showed neat rows of cells.
senses.exampleCN: 在显微镜下，洋葱表皮显出一排排整齐的细胞。
senses.why: Greek skopein meant to look, so with mikros small the compound literally names a way of looking at what the eye cannot see, and the instrument inherited that name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 skopein 意为「看」，与表示「小」的 mikros 组合，字面上就是「观看小东西的方式」，仪器便继承了这个名字。

senses.title: A high-power instrument using electrons or other radiation
senses.definition: any of the more powerful instruments that form an image with electron beams or other radiation instead of ordinary light
senses.definitionCN: 用电子束或其他辐射代替普通光成像的更高倍率的各类显微设备
senses.example: An electron microscope revealed the virus in fine detail.
senses.exampleCN: 电子显微镜把病毒的细节清晰地显现出来。
senses.why: When glass lenses reached their limit, the same word was stretched to instruments that no longer use light, because the purpose rather than the optics is what the name marks.
senses.whyCN: 当玻璃透镜放大到极限，这个词又被延伸到不再用光的仪器上，因为命名看重的是用途，而不是光学原理。

senses.title: Close, searching examination
senses.definition: a situation of being examined very closely, as in the fixed phrase under the microscope
senses.definitionCN: 处于被极为仔细检查的境地，常见于 under the microscope 这一说法
senses.example: After the leak, the whole department was under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 泄密事件之后，整个部门都处在严密审视之下。
senses.why: A microscope exposes what is invisible to the naked eye, so putting a person or an institution under one means even the smallest faults are being looked at.
senses.whyCN: 显微镜把肉眼看不见的东西摊开，因此把人或机构放在显微镜下，就等于连最细小的毛病都要被看清。

intro.en: Microscope joins two Greek words, small and to look, was given a modern Latin form, and entered English in the seventeenth century as lens-making improved.
intro.cn: microscope 把两个希腊词「小」与「看」接在一起，先有近代拉丁语形式，再在十七世纪透镜工艺进步时进入英语。

items.en: Mikros meant small, and it supplied the first element for instruments that work at a scale the eye cannot reach.
items.cn: mikros 意为小的，为那些在人眼够不着的尺度上工作的仪器提供了第一个词素。

items.en: Skopein meant to look at or examine, and its combining form -scope later named many viewing instruments.
items.cn: skopein 意为看、察看，它的构词形式 -scope 后来命名了许多观察仪器。

items.en: Early scientists gave the new instrument a Latin name from the two Greek elements before any English word existed for it.
items.cn: 早期的科学家用这两个希腊词素给新仪器起了拉丁名，当时英语里还没有对应的词。

items.en: English adopted the word in the seventeenth century as lens grinding made single-lens instruments practical for naturalists.
items.cn: 十七世纪，随着透镜研磨技术让单透镜仪器对博物学者变得实用，英语采纳了这个词。

items.en: The compound now covers electron and other advanced instruments, and its prepositional phrase has become a metaphor for close scrutiny.
items.cn: 这个复合词现在涵盖了电子显微镜等进阶设备，它的介词短语也成了「严密审视」的比喻说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the small plus look pattern and its derived family; the near-meaning group collects the glass and the specimens that go with the instrument.
note.cn: 形近组顺着「小」加「看」的构词模式与派生词族；近义组收与这种仪器配套的镜片和标本。

entries.definition: Too small to be seen without an instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 小到不用仪器就看不见的。

entries.definition: The technique of examining things with a microscope.
entries.definitionCN: 用显微镜检查事物的技术。

entries.definition: An instrument for viewing distant objects.
entries.definitionCN: 观察远处物体的仪器。

entries.definition: An instrument for looking over or around an obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 越过或绕过障碍观察的仪器。

entries.definition: A curved piece of glass that bends light to form an image.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲的玻璃片，使光折射成像。

entries.definition: A hand-held lens used to make small things look larger.
entries.definitionCN: 手持透镜，把小的东西放大来看。

entries.definition: A thin glass plate on which a specimen is placed for viewing.
entries.definitionCN: 放置标本供观察的薄玻璃片。

entries.definition: A small sample of something kept for study.
entries.definitionCN: 留作研究用的少量样品。

normalIntro.en: Small plus looking: the compound names an instrument that does not enlarge the object but brings it close enough for the eye.
normalIntro.cn: 「小」加「看」：这个复合词命名的仪器并不把物体变大，而是把它拉到眼睛够得近的地方。

normal.en: Micro- means small and -scope comes from the Greek verb for looking, so the word spells out looking at small things.
normal.cn: micro- 意为「小」，-scope 出自希腊语中表示「看」的动词，这个词把「看小东西」直接拼了出来。

normal.en: Telescope uses the same -scope element for far objects, and periscope uses it for looking around.
normal.cn: telescope 用同一个 -scope 词素看远处，periscope 用它绕过障碍看。

normal.en: Microscopic adds -ic and describes what is too small for the unaided eye.
normal.cn: microscopic 加了 -ic，形容小到肉眼无法看清的东西。

normal.en: Microscopy names the technique, and a microscopist is the person who performs it.
normal.cn: microscopy 指这门技术，microscopist 指操作它的人。

normal.en: Under the microscope is a fixed phrase that moved from the lab bench into everyday talk about scrutiny.
normal.cn: under the microscope 是固定说法，已经从实验台走进日常语言，指严密审查。

abstract.en: The glass does not enlarge the cell; it only shortens the distance between the cell and your attention.
abstract.cn: 镜片并不把细胞变大，只是缩短了细胞与你注意力之间的距离。

abstract.en: Looking closely rewrites what you see: a plain leaf becomes rows of green rooms.
abstract.cn: 凑近看会改写你所见的：一片普通的叶子变成一排排绿色的小房间。

abstract.en: A lens became a word for scrutiny, because attention magnifies faults just as glass magnifies cells.
abstract.cn: 一片镜片变成了「审视」的代名词，因为注意力放大过失，就像镜片放大细胞一样。

examples.en: The students took turns looking through the microscope.
examples.cn: 学生们轮流透过显微镜观察。

examples.en: An electron microscope can show the shape of a virus.
examples.cn: 电子显微镜能显示病毒的形状。

examples.en: After the audit, the whole office was under the microscope.
examples.cn: 审计之后，整个办公室都处在严密审视之下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克看」——麦克凑近镜片看小虫，看小东西的镜子就是显微镜。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小）与 skopein（看）拼接，经近代科学拉丁语 microscopium 进入英语，指观察微小物体的仪器；没有可靠的古典拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is looking at what is too small; the senses divide into the lens instrument, the powered instruments that replaced light, and the scrutiny those instruments symbolize.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「观看过小的东西」；义项分到透镜仪器、取代光的强力设备，以及这类仪器所象征的严密审视。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single lens bringing the cells of a leaf close enough for the eye.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚镜片把叶片上的细胞拉到眼前。

branches.en: onion cells lined up under a lens
branches.cn: 透镜下排成行的洋葱细胞

branches.en: an electron beam tracing a virus
branches.cn: 电子束扫出病毒的轮廓

branches.en: a department watched after a leak
branches.cn: 泄密之后被盯住的部门

branches.en: detail revealed first by light and then by electrons
branches.cn: 细节先由光显现，再由电子显现

branches.en: the same act of looking closely, at cells and at people
branches.cn: 同一个凑近细看的动作，一次对细胞，一次对人

intro.en: A Greek prefix for small and a Greek look-element form the word, and English suffixes later build the technique and the person around it.
intro.cn: 一个表示「小」的希腊前缀与一个表示「看」的希腊词素构成这个词，英语后缀后来又在它周围造出技术与人的名称。

latinIntro.en: The word was formed from Greek elements and given a modern Latin shape by early scientists, so no classical Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词由希腊词素构成，早期科学家只给了它一个近代拉丁语外形，古典拉丁语中没有同族词记录。

definition_zh: 中间的；中段的；中部的；（用于复合词）中……
definition_en: occupying the middle part of a period, place, range or process, used chiefly in compounds and fixed phrases
core_image: 一条绳子在正中央打了个结，两端朝相反方向延伸出去
scene: 钟声刚过半程，山路上的人停在路中央，抬头核对绳索有没有松。The climber paused in mid-air to check the rope before the next move.
sceneCN: 这里 mid 是「悬在半空、处在中间位置」的意思（第 2 个义项：空间或位置的中间）；句意为攀爬者在半空中停了一下，检查绳索再继续往上。画面里可抓住的物件：岩壁、绳索、路中央的小标牌。

pos.zh: 中间的；中段的；中部的；用于复合词指中部

collocations.zh: 二十世纪九十年代中期

derivatives.zh: 由 mid 与 point 复合，义为「中点」
由 mid 与 week 复合，义为「一周的中间、周三前后」
由 mid 与 section 复合，义为「中部；身体的中段」
由 mid 与 field 复合，义为「中场区域」

senses.title: Halfway through a period of time
senses.definition: in the middle part of a month, year, decade or other stretch of time
senses.definitionCN: 位于某个月、某一年、某个十年等一段时间的中间部分
senses.example: The store is busiest in mid-December.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在十二月中旬最忙。
senses.why: The oldest form of the word simply meant middle, so the first place it settled was time: a point that cuts a long stretch into two halves, as in mid-December and the mid-1990s.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的形式本义就是「中间」，所以它最先固定下来的用法是时间：一个把整段时间分成两半的位置，于是有 mid-December 与 the mid-1990s 这样的说法。

senses.title: The middle of a place or space
senses.definition: located in the central part of a space, especially while in the air or over water
senses.definitionCN: 处在某个空间的中央部分，尤指悬在空中或水面之上
senses.example: The bird hovered in mid-air above the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟在湖面上方的半空中悬停。
senses.why: Because mid marks a point between two ends, it naturally describes a body held between ground and sky, or between two shores; joining it to air keeps the short word usable on its own.
senses.whyCN: 因为 mid 标记的是两端之间的一个位置，所以它顺理成章地用来形容悬在地面与天空之间、或两岸之间的物体；与 air 连用，则让这个短词能够独立出现。

senses.title: Partway through an action or process
senses.definition: while an action or event is already under way and has not yet finished
senses.definitionCN: 在一个动作或事件已经开始、尚未结束的时候
senses.example: She stood up in mid-sentence and left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她话说到一半就站起来离开了房间。
senses.why: An action also has a beginning and an end, so the same midpoint applies to speech, flight or a match; mid-sentence and mid-flight are direct extensions of the time sense.
senses.whyCN: 动作同样有开头和结尾，同一个「中间点」便顺延到说话、飞行或比赛之中；mid-sentence 与 mid-flight 都是时间义的直接延伸。

senses.title: In the middle of a range or scale
senses.definition: of a size, price or level, positioned between the low and high ends
senses.definitionCN: 指尺寸、价格或水平处在低端与高端之间
senses.example: They chose a mid-range phone rather than the most expensive one.
senses.exampleCN: 他们选了一部中档手机，而不是最贵的那款。
senses.why: A scale is laid out like a line with two ends, so mid can name the band in between; that is why shops and ratings say mid-range and mid-level instead of coining another adjective.
senses.whyCN: 等级序列像一条有两个端点的线，mid 因而能指中间那一档；商店与评级说 mid-range、mid-level 而不另造形容词，正是这个道理。

senses.title: Forming compounds for the middle part
senses.titleCN: 构成复合词指某物的中部
senses.definition: used as the first element of compounds that name the central part of a place, body or organization
senses.definitionCN: 作复合词的第一部分，用来指某个地点、身体部位或组织的中部
senses.example: The midfielder ran back to help the defence.
senses.exampleCN: 那名中场球员跑回来协助防守。
senses.why: English often presses a short adjective into service as a prefix; mid joined field, week and section to name the central zone without inventing a new root for each one.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一个短形容词直接拿来当前缀；mid 与 field、week、section 组合，指出中间那块区域，而不必为每个概念另造词根。

intro.en: Mid is one of the oldest words in English; it descends from a reconstructed root for middle and has a genuine Latin cousin in medius.
intro.cn: mid 是英语中最古老的词之一，源自一个表示「中间」的重构词根，并在拉丁语里有真正的同族词 medius。

items.en: The reconstructed root *medhyo- meant middle, and Latin medius also grew from it; the asterisk marks a form rebuilt by linguists, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 重构词根 *medhyo- 意为「中间」，拉丁语 medius 也出自它；星号表示这是语言学家重建的形式，并非有记录的原词。

items.en: The Germanic branch kept the root as *midjaz, which entered Old English with the same meaning.
items.cn: 日耳曼语族把这词根保留为 *midjaz，带着相同的「中间」义进入古英语。

items.en: Old English midd worked as both adjective and noun, and it already formed compounds such as middæg, the middle of the day.
items.cn: 古英语的 midd 可作形容词和名词，并且已经构成 middæg 这类复合词，指一天的中段。

items.en: Middle English shortened the adjective to mid and placed it chiefly before another word, as in midwinter and midnight.
items.cn: 中古英语把形容词缩为 mid，主要把它放在另一个词前面使用，如 midwinter 与 midnight。

items.en: Modern English keeps mid almost entirely in compounds and hyphenated phrases such as mid-air, mid-July and mid-range.
items.cn: 现代英语几乎只在复合词和带连字符的短语里保留 mid，如 mid-air、mid-July 与 mid-range。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same middle root; the near-meaning group collects words for the central point or position.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「中间」词根上的形式；近义组收表示中心点或居中位置的词。

entries.definition: The middle of a group or event; it survives mainly in the phrase in the midst of.
entries.definitionCN: 指人群或事件的中部，主要保留在 in the midst of 这一短语中。

entries.definition: In the middle of something, especially a crowd or a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 在……之中，尤指处于人群或某种情境当中。

entries.definition: Halfway between two places or points.
entries.definitionCN: 在两处或两点之间的中途。

entries.definition: The central part of a country, away from the coast.
entries.definitionCN: 一国远离海岸的中部内陆地区。

entries.definition: At or near the middle of something.
entries.definitionCN: 位于或接近某物的中间。

entries.definition: Coming between two points, levels or stages.
entries.definitionCN: 处在两个位置、等级或阶段之间的。

entries.definition: At the midpoint between two places or stages.
entries.definitionCN: 在两处或两个阶段的中点。

entries.definition: Being the middle value in an ordered set of numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 在一组按序排列的数值中居中的。

normalIntro.en: Mid is the short form of an old English word for middle, and the family around it keeps pointing at the place where two halves meet.
normalIntro.cn: mid 是古英语中表示「中间」的词的短形式，围绕它的一族词始终指向两半相接的地方。

normal.en: Mid is the shortened form of an Old English word for middle, so its own meaning needs no separate explanation.
normal.cn: mid 是古英语「中间」一词的缩写形式，它本身的含义无需另作解释。

normal.en: The word prefers company: mid-July, mid-air and mid-range all place it before the thing that is being halved.
normal.cn: 这个词偏好结伴出现：mid-July、mid-air 与 mid-range 都把它放在被分成两半的事物前面。

normal.en: Latin medius is a true cousin, linking mid to words such as median and intermediate.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 medius 是它真正的同族词，把 mid 与 median、intermediate 一类词连在一起。

normal.en: Mid keeps its hyphen when the compound is new or a number follows, as in mid-1990s and mid-sentence.
normal.cn: 当复合词较新或后面接数字时，mid 保留连字符，如 mid-1990s 与 mid-sentence。

normal.en: Compare midday and midnight: the same mid points at noon on one side and at the darkest hour on the other.
normal.cn: 对比 midday 与 midnight：同一个 mid 一边指向正午，一边指向夜里最深的时刻。

abstract.en: Picture a rope tied at its exact centre; everything named with mid hangs from that knot.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳子在正中央打了个结，凡是用 mid 命名的东西都挂在这个结上。

abstract.en: Mid is a hinge word: it never points at an end, only at the place where two halves meet.
abstract.cn: mid 是个铰链式的词：它从不指向端点，只指向两半相接的地方。

abstract.en: A stadium full of people, a flight over the sea, a decade half spent: one small word holds all these middles.
abstract.cn: 坐满人的体育场、飞越海面的航班、过了一半的十年：一个小词装下了所有这些「中间」。

examples.en: The store is busiest in mid-December.
examples.cn: 这家店在十二月中旬最忙。

examples.en: The bird hovered in mid-air above the lake.
examples.cn: 那只鸟在湖面上方的半空中悬停。

examples.en: They chose a mid-range phone.
examples.cn: 他们选了一部中档手机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密的」——位置卡在正当中的那一点，密得两边一样远；记住 mid 是中间。

root: 古英语 midd（中间）来自原始日耳曼语 *midjaz，更早可追到重构词根 *medhyo-；拉丁语 medius（中间的）是同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core idea is the point between two ends; the senses apply it to time, space, an action in progress, a scale, and compounds naming a middle part.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两端之间的那个点；各义项依次把它用到时间、空间、进行中的动作、等级序列，以及指中部地带的复合词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope tied at its exact centre, both ends running away in opposite directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条绳子在正中央打了结，两端朝相反方向延伸出去。

branches.en: a calendar page folded at the centre of July
branches.cn: 日历翻到七月正中那一页

branches.en: a body hanging between sky and water
branches.cn: 悬在天空与水面之间的身体

branches.en: a sentence cut off before its last word
branches.cn: 话没说完就被截断的一句

branches.en: a row of phones with the middle price tag picked out
branches.cn: 一排手机里被挑出的中间价签

branches.en: a player standing between defence and attack
branches.cn: 站在防守与进攻之间的球员

intro.en: Mid is a free-standing adjective only in older English; today it works mainly as a combining element, and its Latin cousin medius explains the wider family of middle words.
intro.cn: mid 只在较早的英语里独立作形容词；今天它主要作为构词成分，而拉丁同族词 medius 解释了更广的「中间」词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 正午；中午；正午前后
definition_en: the middle of the day around twelve o'clock, the hours on either side of noon, or the light and heat of that moment
core_image: 太阳升到头顶，街上的人影缩成脚边一小团
scene: 太阳升到头顶，集市上的遮阳棚把地面压出一圈窄影，摊主收起秤准备吃饭。At midday the market square was almost empty.
sceneCN: 这里 midday 是「正午」（第 1 个义项：一天的正中、十二点前后）；句意为正午时集市广场几乎空了。画面里可抓住的物件：遮阳棚、窄影、收起的秤。

derivatives.zh: 同以 mid- 前缀构成，指下午的中段

senses.title: The middle of the day
senses.definition: twelve o'clock in the middle of the day, when the sun stands highest
senses.definitionCN: 一天的正中，即太阳升到最高处的十二点前后
senses.example: The bells rang at midday.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时分钟声响起。
senses.why: Old English middæg is literally mid plus day, so the word began as a label for the point that splits the day in two; noon is exactly that point.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 middæg 字面就是 mid 加 day，这个词最初只是给「把一天切成两半」的那个位置贴标签；正午恰恰就是那个位置。

senses.title: The hours around noon
senses.definition: the period on either side of noon, when people eat and rest
senses.definitionCN: 正午前后的一段时间，人们在这时吃饭、歇息
senses.example: The square stays busy through midday.
senses.exampleCN: 广场在整个中午时段都很热闹。
senses.why: Once the word names the peak of the day, it easily widens to the hours that surround the peak, because meals and rests cluster around that moment.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指到一天的最高点，就很容易扩展到围绕这个点的那几个小时，因为吃饭与休息都集中在那个时段。

senses.title: The strongest light and heat of the day
senses.definition: the bright, hot quality of the day at its height
senses.definitionCN: 一天走到最高处时那种明亮、炎热的特质
senses.example: The cactus folds its flowers against the midday sun.
senses.exampleCN: 仙人掌把花收拢起来，以避开正午的烈日。
senses.why: Because the sun stands highest then, midday also names the glare and heat of that moment; the word shifts from a clock reading to a felt condition.
senses.whyCN: 因为太阳此时最高，midday 也指那一刻的强光与炎热；词义便从钟点读数转到身体感受到的状态。

senses.title: Happening at noon
senses.definition: used before a noun for something that takes place or appears at noon
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指在正午发生或出现的事物
senses.example: They packed a midday meal for the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为长途步行准备了一顿午餐。
senses.why: English lets a time noun sit before another noun like an adjective; midday meal and midday break simply compress at midday into a single word, with no change of form.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许时间名词像形容词一样放在另一个名词前；midday meal 与 midday break 只是把 at midday 压缩成一个词，形式并没有变化。

intro.en: Midday is an ancient compound: the root for middle was joined to the word for day before English existed as a separate language.
intro.cn: midday 是一个古老的复合词：在英语尚未成为独立语言之前，表示「中间」的词根就已经和表示「日」的词连在一起了。

items.en: The compound *midjadagaz joined the root for middle to the word for day, so the middle of the day was named as one unit.
items.cn: *midjadagaz 把表示「中间」的词根与表示「日」的词连成一个单位，一天的正中由此有了专门的名字。

items.en: Old English middæg carried the compound into daily use alongside midd, and it named the point where morning and afternoon meet.
items.cn: 古英语的 middæg 与 midd 一起进入日常使用，用来指上午与下午交会的那一点。

items.en: Middle English kept midday as the name of the noon hour and began to place it before other nouns, as in midday meal.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 midday 指正午时刻，并开始把它放在其他名词前面，如 midday meal。

items.en: Writers of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries extended midday to the surrounding hours and to the heat and glare of noon.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的作者把 midday 扩展到正午前后的几个小时，也用来指正午的炎热与强光。

items.en: Modern English uses midday for noon, for the hours around it, and attributively in compounds such as midday sun and midday break.
items.cn: 现代英语用 midday 指正午、指正午前后，也作定语用于 midday sun、midday break 之类的复合说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds made with the same mid prefix; the near-meaning group collects other names for noon and the lunch hour.
note.cn: 形近组收用同一个 mid 前缀构成的复合词；近义组收其他表示正午与午饭时段的说法。

entries.definition: The middle part of the morning.

entries.definition: The middle part of the afternoon.

entries.definition: The middle of the day; this word is built on noon rather than on mid, so it is only close in spelling and meaning.
