entries.definition: Twelve o'clock in the day.
entries.definitionCN: 白天的十二点；正午。

entries.definition: The period around noon.
entries.definitionCN: 正午前后的一段时间。

entries.definition: The time when people eat their midday meal.
entries.definitionCN: 人们吃午饭的时间。

normalIntro.en: Midday is a transparent compound of mid and day, and the words around it keep the same recipe of middle plus a unit of time.
normalIntro.cn: midday 是 mid 与 day 组成的透明复合词，它周围的说法也都沿用了「中间加时间单位」的配方。

normal.en: Midday is mid plus day, so the word is a small picture of a day cut in half.
normal.cn: midday 就是 mid 加 day，这个词本身就是「把一天切成两半」的小画面。

normal.en: The main stress falls on the second half, mid-DAY, which is why it sounds like one point rather than two separate words.
normal.cn: 主重音落在后半段 mid-DAY 上，所以它听起来像一个时间点，而不是两个独立的词。

normal.en: Latin meridies, from medius and dies, follows the same recipe: middle plus day.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 meridies 由 medius 与 dies 合成，走的是同一条思路：中间加日。

normal.en: Midday meal and midday sun show the noun acting like an adjective without any added ending.
normal.cn: midday meal 与 midday sun 展示了这个名词不靠任何词尾就充当形容词。

normal.en: Set it beside midnight: the same middle, but on the other side of the clock.
normal.cn: 把它和 midnight 放在一起看：同样是「中间」，只是落在钟面的另一侧。

abstract.en: A shadow shrinking to the feet is the body's own clock announcing midday.
abstract.cn: 影子缩到脚边，就是身体自带的钟在宣告正午。

abstract.en: Midday is the hinge of the day: morning on one side, afternoon on the other.
abstract.cn: midday 是一天的铰链：一边是上午，一边是下午。

abstract.en: Two ideas, middle and day, are stored inside one short sound.
abstract.cn: 「中间」与「日」两个概念，被收进了一个短短的声音里。

examples.en: The bells rang at midday.
examples.cn: 正午时分钟声响起。

examples.en: We spent the whole midday walking through the old town.
examples.cn: 我们整个中午都在老城里走。

examples.en: The cactus folds its flowers against the midday sun.
examples.cn: 仙人掌把花收拢起来，以避开正午的烈日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密的」加「得」——太阳密得头顶发烫，一天正好走到正中；midday 是正午。

root: 古英语 middæg，由 midd（中间）与 dæg（日、天）复合；拉丁语 meridies（medius 中间 + dies 日）用的是同一种构词思路。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the peak of the day; the senses spread out from that point to the noon hour, the hours around it, the heat of the moment, and attributive use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一天的最高点；各义项从这个点扩到正午时刻、前后时段、当时的炎热，以及作定语的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sun directly overhead and a shadow shrunk to the feet.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳正悬在头顶，影子缩到脚边。

branches.en: bells striking as the shadow vanishes
branches.cn: 影子缩到脚边时响起的钟声

branches.en: stalls closing while people rest
branches.cn: 人们歇息、摊子收起的时刻

branches.en: a cactus closing its flowers against the glare
branches.cn: 仙人掌在强光里收拢花朵

branches.en: a packed meal waiting for a long walk
branches.cn: 为长途步行备好的饭盒

branches.en: a market square emptied by heat
branches.cn: 被炎热赶空的集市广场

intro.en: Midday is held together by a middle root and a day noun, and Latin built its own word for noon from exactly the same two ideas.
intro.cn: midday 由表示「中间」的词根和表示「日」的名词合成，拉丁语用完全相同的两个概念造出了自己的「正午」。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 中间；中部；中期；腰部；中间的；中等的；中间派的
definition_en: the central point or part of something, the middle period of a process, the waist, or an adjective meaning central or moderate
core_image: 一条长桌的正中摆着一只花瓶，两侧的椅子对称排开
scene: 长桌两端都坐满了人，只有正中的位置还空着，等着最后到的那位客人。She cut the cake down the middle and gave half to each child.
sceneCN: 这里 middle 是「中间、正中」（第 1 个义项：距离两边同样远的位置）；句意为她沿着正中把蛋糕切开，分给每个孩子一半。画面里可抓住的物件：长桌、空着的正中座位、切开的蛋糕。

pos.zh: 中间的；中等的；中间派的

derivatives.zh: 由 middle 加 -ing 构成，义为「中等的、还过得去的」
由 middle 与 man 复合，义为「中间商；中介」
由 middle 与 weight 复合，指拳击的中量级
由 middle 与 brow 复合，指品味中庸的（人）

senses.title: The central point or part
senses.definition: the point or area equally far from the edges or ends of something
senses.definitionCN: 距离边缘或两端同样远的那一点或那一带
senses.example: There is a fountain in the middle of the square.
senses.exampleCN: 广场中央有一座喷泉。
senses.why: Old English middel was built with the suffix -el from a root for middle, much as a small tool is made from a larger one; the word names the place that divides a length into equal halves.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 middel 由表示「中间」的词根加后缀 -el 构成，就像用一个较大物件做出小工具；这个词指的就是把一段长度分成相等两半的位置。

senses.title: The middle of a period or process
senses.definition: a point in time when an event or process is half done
senses.definitionCN: 一个事件或过程进行到一半的时间点
senses.example: The project ran into trouble in the middle of the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目在夏季中期遇到了麻烦。
senses.why: Because the central point can be laid on time as well as on space, the same word covers the halfway stage of a season, a story or a negotiation.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个中心点既能放在空间上，也能放在时间上，同一个词便覆盖了季节、故事或谈判进行到一半的阶段。

senses.title: The waist
senses.definition: the narrow part of the body between the chest and the hips, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指胸部与臀部之间身体较窄的部分
senses.example: He tied the rope around his middle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把绳子系在腰上。
senses.why: A body is widest at the shoulders and hips and narrows between them, so the word for the central part came to name the waist with no metaphor beyond shape.
senses.whyCN: 人的身体在肩与臀处最宽，中间收窄，于是表示「中部」的词就用来指腰，除了形状之外并没有额外的比喻。

senses.title: Halfway between two positions
senses.definition: placed or ranked between two other things, neither first nor last
senses.definitionCN: 处在另外两者之间，既不在最前也不在最后
senses.example: Put the tallest child in the middle row.
senses.exampleCN: 把最高的孩子安排在中间那一排。
senses.why: The noun turned adjective by standing before another noun; middle row simply means the row that sits between the front and the back.
senses.whyCN: 名词放到另一个名词前面就转成了形容词；middle row 指的就是夹在最前与最后之间的那一排。

senses.title: Moderate in politics or opinion
senses.definition: holding views that avoid the extremes of left and right, or of any strong division
senses.definitionCN: 持避免左右极端或任何强烈对立的观点
senses.example: The paper speaks to middle voters who dislike both extremes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸面向不喜欢两个极端的中间选民。
senses.why: A political spectrum is imagined as a line with two ends, so the party or voter near its centre is called middle; the spatial image is simply carried into public life.
senses.whyCN: 政治光谱被想象成一条有两个端点的线，靠近中心位置的党派或选民就被称为 middle；空间的形象就这样搬进了公共生活。

intro.en: Middle is the full form of the old root that also gives the short word mid; its history runs from a prehistoric root, through Old English, into everyday modern senses such as waist and moderate politics.
intro.cn: middle 是古老词根的完整形式，短词 mid 也出自同一来源；它的历史从史前词根出发，经古英语，一直走到今天「腰部」与「温和政治」这类日常义项。

items.en: The reconstructed root *medhyo- meant middle and is the common ancestor of English middle and Latin medius.
items.cn: 重构词根 *medhyo- 意为「中间」，是英语 middle 与拉丁语 medius 的共同祖先。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed as *midilaz or *medilaz, a noun and adjective for the central part of something.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中的形式一般重构为 *midilaz 或 *medilaz，是表示某物中部的名词与形容词。

items.en: Old English middel added the suffix -el to the root, giving a full adjective and noun beside the shorter midd.
items.cn: 古英语 middel 在词根后加后缀 -el，在较短的 midd 之外提供了一个完整的形容词与名词。

items.en: Middle English kept middel and middle side by side, and the noun already covered space, time and the human waist.
items.cn: 中古英语中 middel 与 middle 并行使用，名词已经同时覆盖空间、时间与人的腰部。

items.en: Modern English settled on middle, extended it to social and political moderation, and kept it in fixed phrases such as middle class and middle age.
items.cn: 现代英语最终确定拼写为 middle，把词义扩展到社会与政治的温和立场，并保留在 middle class、middle age 这类固定说法中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin middle root or merely close in spelling; the near-meaning group collects other words for the centre.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「中间」词根上的词，或仅仅拼写相近的词；近义组收其他表示中心的词。

entries.definition: To interfere in something that is not one's business; it is unrelated to middle and only looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 干涉与自己无关的事；它与 middle 没有词源关系，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: Situated in the middle, especially in anatomy.
entries.definitionCN: 位于中间的，尤用于解剖学。

entries.definition: The middle value in an ordered set, or a line through the middle.
entries.definitionCN: 有序数值中的中间值，或经过中点的线。

entries.definition: Something in the middle, such as a middle size or a means of communication.
entries.definitionCN: 处于中间的事物，如中号尺寸或传播媒介。

entries.definition: The exact middle point of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的正中心点。

entries.definition: The exact middle point of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的正中心点。

entries.definition: The central and most important part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物最中心、最重要的部分。

entries.definition: A point exactly halfway between two ends.
entries.definitionCN: 正好位于两端中间的点。

normalIntro.en: Middle is the long form of the old middle root, and its family keeps returning to the idea of a point that divides a whole into equal parts.
normalIntro.cn: middle 是古老「中间」词根的完整形式，它的一族词反复回到同一个想法：把整体分成相等两部分的那一点。

normal.en: Middle is the full form beside the short mid, the way middle school is longer than midterm.
normal.cn: middle 是短词 mid 的完整形式，就像 middle school 比 midterm 更长一样。

normal.en: Old English added -el to the root, a suffix that also appears in words for small tools, so middle is a built form rather than a bare root.
normal.cn: 古英语在词根后加了 -el，这个后缀也出现在表示小工具的词汇里，所以 middle 是构造出来的形式，而不是光秃秃的词根。

normal.en: Latin medius is a genuine cousin, which links middle to medial, median and medium.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 medius 是真正的同族词，把 middle 与 medial、median、medium 连在一起。

normal.en: The phrases middle class and middle age show how easily the spatial word moves into social life.
normal.cn: middle class 与 middle age 展示了这个空间词多么容易走进社会生活。

normal.en: In the middle of is the everyday frame: whatever follows it is the thing being cut into two halves.
normal.cn: in the middle of 是日常框架：后面接的东西，就是被分成两半的那件事。

abstract.en: A vase placed at the exact centre of a long table turns the table into two equal halves.
abstract.cn: 花瓶摆在长桌的正中央，桌子就被分成了两个相等的半边。

abstract.en: Middle is a balancing word: it keeps both ends at the same distance and refuses to choose.
abstract.cn: middle 是个平衡词：它让两端保持同等距离，拒绝偏向任何一边。

abstract.en: From a row of seats to a political debate, the same centre keeps being found and named.
abstract.cn: 从一排座位到一场政治辩论，同一个中心不断被找到、被命名。

examples.en: There is a fountain in the middle of the square.
examples.cn: 广场中央有一座喷泉。

examples.en: The project ran into trouble in the middle of the summer.
examples.cn: 这个项目在夏季中期遇到了麻烦。

examples.en: Put the tallest child in the middle row.
examples.cn: 把最高的孩子安排在中间那一排。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米的」——长桌正中的花瓶离两边一样远，米尺量到一半就叫 middle。

root: 古英语 middel，由表示「中间」的词根加后缀 -el 构成，更早来自原始日耳曼语 *midilaz；拉丁语 medius（中间的）为同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the point equally far from both ends; the senses carry that point into space, time, the body, a rank, and the moderate centre of politics.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是距离两端同样远的那一点；各义项把这个点带进空间、时间、身体、名次，以及政治上的温和中间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vase at the exact centre of a long table, with chairs arranged evenly on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌正中央摆着一只花瓶，两侧椅子均匀排开。

branches.en: a fountain standing where the paths cross
branches.cn: 立在道路交会处的喷泉

branches.en: a project stalling halfway through summer
branches.cn: 在夏季过半时停滞的工程

branches.en: a rope tied around a narrow waist
branches.cn: 系在窄腰上的绳子

branches.en: a child seated between the front and back rows
branches.cn: 坐在前排与后排之间的孩子

branches.en: a voter standing between two shouting camps
branches.cn: 夹在两个高声阵营之间的选民

intro.en: Middle is a root plus an old suffix, and the same Latin root medius supplied a whole range of words about centres and middles.
intro.cn: middle 是词根加一个古老后缀，而同一个拉丁词根 medius 提供了整批表示中心与中间的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 午夜；子夜；午夜十二点；深夜；午夜的
definition_en: twelve o'clock at night, the quiet hours around it, the deepest darkness of the night, or attributive use before another noun
core_image: 钟面两根指针叠在最高处，窗外一片深黑
scene: 最后一班车开走后，站台上只剩一盏灯，钟声刚敲过整点，整条街都沉进黑暗里。The train left the station at midnight, and the platform fell silent.
sceneCN: 这里 midnight 是「午夜十二点」（第 1 个义项：一天结束、下一天开始的整点）；句意为列车在午夜离站，站台随之安静下来。画面里可抓住的物件：站台灯、末班车、钟面。

pos.zh: 午夜；子夜；午夜十二点；深夜

derivatives.zh: 由 midnight 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「午夜的、深夜般的」，属文学罕用说法
与 midnight 同用 mid- 前缀，指仲夏、夏至前后
与 midnight 同用 mid- 前缀，指仲冬、冬至前后

senses.title: Twelve o'clock at night
senses.definition: the exact moment when one day ends and the next begins
senses.definitionCN: 一天结束、下一天开始的那一刹那
senses.example: The clock struck midnight before anyone spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 还没人开口，钟就敲响了午夜十二点。
senses.why: Old English midniht is mid plus niht, the middle of the night; it first marked the point halfway between sunset and sunrise, and the clock later fixed that middle at twelve.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 midniht 就是 mid 加 niht，即「夜的正中」；它最初标记的是日落到日出之间的中点，后来钟表把这个中点固定在十二点。

senses.title: The quiet hours around twelve
senses.definition: the hours on either side of twelve, when most people are asleep
senses.definitionCN: 十二点前后的一段时间，多数人已经入睡
senses.example: Guards change shifts around midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵在午夜前后换班。
senses.why: Once the word names the darkest point, it also covers the still hours that surround it, because sleep and silence gather on both sides of twelve.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指到夜的最深处，也就覆盖了围绕它的那几个寂静小时，因为睡眠与安静都在十二点两侧聚集。

senses.title: The deepest darkness of the night
senses.definition: the deep darkness of night, or a figurative moment of greatest gloom
senses.definitionCN: 夜的深沉黑暗，也比喻最阴沉、最低落的时刻
senses.example: The village lay in midnight darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 村子陷在深夜的黑暗里。
senses.why: Because midnight is the point farthest from daylight, writers use it for any moment of deepest darkness or despair, moving from clock time to feeling.
senses.whyCN: 因为午夜是离白昼最远的时刻，作家便用它指任何最黑暗、最绝望的关头，词义从钟点时间转向情绪。

senses.title: Happening at twelve at night
senses.definition: used before a noun for something that occurs or appears at midnight
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指在午夜发生或出现的事物
senses.example: They caught the midnight train to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搭上午夜的列车去海边。
senses.why: A time noun placed before another noun works like an adjective; midnight train and midnight snack simply shorten at midnight without changing the word's form.
senses.whyCN: 时间名词放在另一个名词前就像形容词；midnight train 与 midnight snack 只是把 at midnight 压缩，词形并未改变。

intro.en: Midnight is an old compound of the middle root and the word for night, and its meaning has moved from the midpoint of darkness to the fixed hour of the clock.
intro.cn: midnight 是「中间」词根与「夜」组成的古老复合词，含义已从黑暗的中点移到钟表上固定的整点。

items.en: The compound is reconstructed as *midjanahts, middle plus night, a label for the centre of the dark hours.
items.cn: 这个复合词一般重构为 *midjanahts，即「中间」加「夜」，用来标记黑暗时段的中心。

items.en: Old English midniht kept that shape and named the middle of the night rather than a point on any instrument.
items.cn: 古英语的 midniht 保留了这一结构，指夜的正中，而不是任何仪器上的刻度。

items.en: Middle English midnight stayed close to the older sense while clocks began to divide the night into equal hours.
items.cn: 中古英语的 midnight 仍贴近较早的含义，而与此同时钟表开始把夜晚划成等长的时辰。

items.en: Once mechanical clocks were common, midnight settled at twelve, the moment that separates one calendar day from the next.
items.cn: 机械钟普及之后，midnight 固定在十二点，成为把一个日历日与下一个分开的那一刻。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative sense of deepest gloom and the attributive use seen in midnight train and midnight snack.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「最深的阴郁」这一比喻义，以及 midnight train、midnight snack 中可见的定语用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built with the same mid or night material; the near-meaning group collects phrases for the dead of night.
note.cn: 形近组收用同一个 mid 或 night 材料构成的词；近义组收表示深夜的说法。

entries.definition: Happening or appearing at midnight; a rare, literary adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 在午夜发生或出现的；罕用的文学形容词。

entries.definition: The middle of summer, around the longest day.
entries.definitionCN: 夏季的正中，约在白昼最长的那几天。

entries.definition: The middle of winter, around the shortest day.
entries.definitionCN: 冬季的正中，约在白昼最短的那几天。

entries.definition: The middle of the week, around Wednesday.
entries.definitionCN: 一周的中间，约在周三前后。

entries.definition: The late night hours when magic was once thought to be strongest.
entries.definitionCN: 深夜时分，旧时被认为魔法最强的时刻。

entries.definition: The darkest and quietest part of the night.
entries.definitionCN: 夜里最黑、最安静的时候。

entries.definition: The hours after midnight, usually between one and four.
entries.definitionCN: 午夜之后的凌晨时分，通常指一点到四点。

normalIntro.en: Midnight is mid plus night, and the family around it keeps joining the middle root to units of time or to the dark half of the day.
normalIntro.cn: midnight 就是 mid 加 night，它周围的一族词不断把「中间」词根接到时间单位或一天中黑暗的那一半上。

normal.en: Midnight is mid plus night, so the word literally says middle of the night.
normal.cn: midnight 就是 mid 加 night，字面说的就是「夜的正中」。

normal.en: Old English wrote it as one word, midniht, which is why the modern spelling has no hyphen or space.
normal.cn: 古英语就把它写成一个词 midniht，所以现代拼写既不加连字符也不留空格。

normal.en: The clock sense is younger than the word: midnight first meant the middle of the dark hours, not the number twelve.
normal.cn: 钟点义比这个词本身年轻：midnight 最初指黑暗时段的中点，而不是数字十二。

normal.en: Burn the midnight oil comes from lamps that burned oil, and it keeps the word tied to late work.
normal.cn: burn the midnight oil 来自点油灯的年代，这个说法把 midnight 牢牢系在深夜劳作上。

normal.en: Set it beside midday: the same middle, but on the dark side of the clock.
normal.cn: 把它和 midday 并排看：同样是「中间」，只是落在钟面偏暗的那一侧。

abstract.en: Two hands stacked at the top of the dial, and the street outside goes completely dark.
abstract.cn: 两根指针叠在表盘最高处，外面的街道彻底暗下来。

abstract.en: Midnight is the seam of the calendar: the old day ends and the new one begins in the same tick.
abstract.cn: midnight 是日历的接缝：旧的一天与新的一天在同一个滴答里交接。

abstract.en: The word moves from a point on a dial to a feeling of total gloom, because both sit as far as possible from daylight.
abstract.cn: 这个词从表盘上的一个点走到「彻底阴郁」的感受，因为两者都离白昼尽可能远。

examples.en: The clock struck midnight before anyone spoke.
examples.cn: 还没人开口，钟就敲响了午夜十二点。

examples.en: Guards change shifts around midnight.
examples.cn: 卫兵在午夜前后换班。

examples.en: They caught the midnight train to the coast.
examples.cn: 他们搭上午夜的列车去海边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密的」加「奈特」——夜密得看不见路，钟点又落到最低处；midnight 是午夜。

root: 古英语 midniht，由 midd（中间）与 niht（夜）复合，一般重构为原始日耳曼语 *midjanahts；拉丁语以 medius（中间）加 nox（夜）构成 media nox，思路相同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the middle of the night; the senses run from the clock hour to the surrounding quiet hours, to figurative darkness, and to attributive use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是夜的正中；各义项从钟表整点，扩到前后的寂静时段、比喻性的黑暗，以及作定语的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands stacked at the top of a clock dial while the street outside is completely dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟面两根指针叠在最高处，外面的街道一片漆黑。

branches.en: a clock striking while a platform empties
branches.cn: 站台空下去时钟声敲响

branches.en: guards trading places in the dark
branches.cn: 卫兵在黑暗里交接

branches.en: a village with no light in any window
branches.cn: 窗里没有一盏灯的村子

branches.en: a last train waiting under one lamp
branches.cn: 一盏灯下等候的末班车

branches.en: travellers hurrying aboard before the doors close
branches.cn: 赶在关门前上车的旅客

intro.en: Midnight joins the middle root to the word for night, and Latin built its own midnight phrase from exactly the same two elements.
intro.cn: midnight 把「中间」词根接到表示「夜」的词上，拉丁语用完全相同的两个成分造出了自己的「午夜」说法。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 可能；也许；（语气委婉）可以；力量；威力
definition_en: used to say that something is possible but not certain; used in careful requests and suggestions; used with have of something that was possible but did not happen; and as a noun, great physical strength
core_image: 一个人攥紧拳头，把全身的力气压进一条绷紧的绳索
scene: 仓库的门被风吹得砰砰作响，几个工人合力抵住一扇即将倒下的木门，肩膀紧紧压住门板。He pushed with all his might against the swinging door.
sceneCN: 这里是「力量、气力」（第 4 个义项：身体的力气）；句意为他用尽全力抵住那扇摇动的门。图中可辨识物件：抵门的肩膀、晃动的门板、仓库门。

derivatives.zh: 由 might 加 -y 构成，义为「强大的；有力的」
由 mighty 去 y 加 -ily 构成，义为「有力地；非常」
由 mighty 去 y 加 -ness 构成，义为「强大；威力」

senses.title: Possibility that something is true or may happen
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible, though the speaker is not certain it is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事有可能发生或成立，但说话人并不确定
senses.example: It might rain before we reach the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到车站之前可能会下雨。
senses.why: Might is the past form of may, and English uses a past form to make a statement sound less sure, so the word moves from permission to a guarded guess.
senses.whyCN: might 是 may 的过去式，而英语常用过去形式让陈述听起来不那么确定，于是这个词从「许可」转向「留有余地的猜测」。

senses.title: A polite request or a hesitant suggestion
senses.definition: used to ask for something or suggest an action in a careful, polite way
senses.definitionCN: 用于小心、客气地提出请求或建议
senses.example: Might I borrow your umbrella for an hour?
senses.exampleCN: 我可以借你的伞用一个小时吗？
senses.why: The same past form softens the demand; by placing the request in a distant tense, the speaker leaves the listener free to refuse.
senses.whyCN: 同一个过去式把要求放软：把请求放进一个较远的时态里，就等于给听者留下拒绝的余地。

senses.title: A past possibility that was not taken
senses.definition: used with have to say that something was possible or should have happened but did not
senses.definitionCN: 与 have 连用，表示某事本来可能发生或本该发生，却没有发生
senses.example: You might have told me the meeting had moved.
senses.exampleCN: 你本可以告诉我会议改了时间。
senses.why: Once might marks unreal possibility, adding have fixes that unreal possibility in the past, and the speaker can point at a road that was open and was not walked.
senses.whyCN: 既然 might 标记「非现实的」可能性，再接上 have 就把这种可能固定在过去，说话人便能指向一条曾经敞开、却没被走的路。

senses.title: Great physical power or strength
senses.definition: great physical strength or force, especially when gathered for a single effort
senses.definitionCN: 巨大的体力或力量，尤指为一次发力而聚集起来
senses.example: He pushed with all his might against the swinging door.
senses.exampleCN: 他用尽全力抵住那扇摇动的门。
senses.why: Before it was a modal verb, might was a noun meaning power, and the noun still keeps the older body sense that the modal has left behind.
senses.whyCN: 在成为情态动词之前，might 本是一个意为「力量」的名词；这个名词至今保留着情态动词早已丢下的、属于身体的那层意思。

intro.en: Might began as an Old English noun for power and as a past form of may, and the two meanings have stayed side by side.
intro.cn: might 起初既是古英语中表示「力量」的名词，又是 may 的过去式，这两种身份一直并存。

items.en: A reconstructed root for being able is generally proposed behind the Germanic words for power, though its exact shape remains uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，日耳曼语中表示「有能力」的词背后有一个重构词根，但其确切形态仍不确定。

items.en: The noun for power stood beside a verb meaning to be able, and the two supplied the family of may and might.
items.cn: 表示力量的名词与表示「有能力」的动词并列存在，二者共同供出了 may 与 might 的词族。

items.en: Old English meaht meant power, strength or ability, and miht was its variant spelling.
items.cn: 古英语 meaht 意为力量、力气、能力，miht 是它的变体拼写。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun might for power while also using it as the past form of may in conditional statements.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词 might 表示力量，同时把它当作 may 的过去式，用在条件句里。

items.en: Modern English made the modal use dominant and left the noun in fixed phrases such as 「with all one's might」.
items.cn: 现代英语让情态动词用法占了主导，名词则退守到「with all one's might」这类固定短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family of may and might plus a compound built on mighty; the near-meaning group collects words for power and for possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收 may 与 might 的同族词，外加一个由 mighty 构成的复合词；近义组收表示力量与表示可能的词。

entries.definition: Very strong or powerful.
entries.definitionCN: 非常强壮或有力量的。

entries.definition: With great force, or very much.
entries.definitionCN: 以巨大的力量，或非常地。

entries.definition: The present form of the modal verb whose past form is might.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词的现在形式，might 是它的过去式。

entries.definition: Having complete power, formed from all and mighty.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有全然的力量，由 all 与 mighty 构成。

entries.definition: The ability to act or to control people and events.
entries.definitionCN: 行动或控制人与事件的能力。

entries.definition: The physical force that a body or a material can use or bear.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或材料能施展、能承受的物理之力。

entries.definition: Energy applied to move something or to make a change happen.
entries.definitionCN: 为移动某物或促成改变而施加的能量。

entries.definition: Another past-form modal used for possibility and for polite requests.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个用过去形式表示可能与委婉请求的情态动词。

normalIntro.en: The word carries two lives, a noun for bodily power and a past form of may; the family keeps returning to what a person is able to do and what may therefore happen.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词身负两重身份：一个是表示身体力量的名词，一个是 may 的过去式；同族词反复回到人能做到什么，以及因此可能发生什么。

normal.en: Might is the past form of may, and English uses a past form to sound less certain.
normal.cn: might 是 may 的过去式，英语用过去形式来让语气显得不那么确定。

normal.en: The noun might meant power long before the modal sense appeared, and the two live on in the same spelling.
normal.cn: 名词 might 在情态用法出现之前就指力量，两种身份共用同一个拼写，一直活到今天。

normal.en: The phrase 「with all one's might」 is the noun in fixed form, where might still means bodily strength.
normal.cn: 「with all one's might」是名词用法的固定形式，这里的 might 仍指身体的力量。

normal.en: Mighty adds -y to might, turning power into an adjective, and mightily adds -ly in turn.
normal.cn: mighty 在 might 后加 -y，把力量变成形容词，mightily 再在其后加 -ly。

normal.en: 「Might have done」 points at a road that was open in the past and was not taken.
normal.cn: 「might have done」指向一条过去曾经敞开、却没有被走的路。

abstract.en: A single word for power and for possibility suggests that what is possible is what a person is able to bring about.
abstract.cn: 一个同时表示力量与可能的词说明：所谓可能，就是人有能力促成的范围。

abstract.en: The modal keeps a past form to sound humble, a reminder that grammar itself can lower a voice.
abstract.cn: 情态动词用过去形式来显得谦逊，这提醒人：语法本身也能把声音放低。

abstract.en: Might have says that history holds unused doors, and the word lets a speaker stand in front of one.
abstract.cn: might have 说明过去握着一些没被推开的门，这个词让说话人站到其中一扇门前。

examples.en: It might rain before we reach the station.
examples.cn: 我们到车站之前可能会下雨。

examples.en: Might I borrow your umbrella for an hour?
examples.cn: 我可以借你的伞用一个小时吗？

examples.en: He pushed with all his might against the swinging door.
examples.cn: 他用尽全力抵住那扇摇动的门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦特」——麦特力气特别大，一拳就能推开门；记住 might 是可能，也是力量。

root: 古英语 meaht（力量、能力）与动词 magan（有能力）同源；作为 may 的过去式，might 又承担「可能」这一情态义。一般认为其更早的词根只能重构，且没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ability, which can become a guarded guess; the senses divide into possibility, polite request, a past chance not taken, and bodily power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「有能力」，它可以长成一句留有余地的猜测；义项分为可能、委婉请求、错过的过去机会，以及身体的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person gripping a rope with both hands and pressing all the strength of the body into it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人攥紧拳头，把全身的力气压进一条绷紧的绳索。

branches.en: shoulders pressed against a shaking warehouse door
branches.cn: 肩膀抵住一扇摇动的仓库门

branches.en: a sky that cannot decide whether to rain
branches.cn: 一片拿不定主意要不要下雨的天

branches.en: a hand raised politely before a question
branches.cn: 提问前礼貌抬起的手

branches.en: a road left unwalked and still visible behind
branches.cn: 一条没被走、却仍在身后可见的路

branches.en: a rope pulled tight and a chance let slip
branches.cn: 绷紧的绳索与溜走的机会

intro.en: The word is carried by an Old English noun of power, the verb beside it, the past form of may, and two English endings that build the adjective and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语中表示力量的名词、与它并列的动词、may 的过去式形式，以及构成形容词与副词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for might: the word belongs to the Germanic branch, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: might 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它属于日耳曼语这一支，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

definition_zh: 轻微的；不严重的；温和的；和善的；暖和的；（味道）淡的
definition_en: not severe or harsh in degree; gentle and kind in manner; warmer than expected for the season; and soft rather than sharp in taste
core_image: 冬日午后，阳光斜照进院子，一只猫在石阶上伸了个懒腰
scene: 冬日的午后阳光斜照进院子，石阶上一点风也没有，老猫在墙根下慢慢伸了个懒腰。The winter here is almost mild enough for the cat to sleep outdoors.
sceneCN: 这里是「天气暖和的、温和的」（第 3 个义项：天气不冷冽）；句意为这里的冬天暖和得几乎能让猫睡在户外。图中可辨识物件：斜照的阳光、石阶、伸懒腰的猫。

pos.zh: 轻微的；温和的；暖和的；味淡的

derivatives.zh: 由 mild 加 -ly 构成，义为「轻微地；温和地」
由 mild 加 -ness 构成，义为「温和；轻微」
由 mild 与 mannered 复合而成，义为「举止温和的」

senses.title: Not severe or harsh in degree
senses.definition: not strong, serious or severe, especially of illness, pain or a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 不强烈、不严重、不厉害，尤用于疾病、疼痛或惩罚
senses.example: He had a mild fever and stayed home for one day.
senses.exampleCN: 他发了低烧，在家待了一天。
senses.why: Old English milde meant gentle and merciful, so this sense measures severity by how little force is used rather than by how much there is.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 milde 意为温和、仁慈，所以这一义项是用「用力之少」来衡量严重程度，而不是看它有多少力量。

senses.title: Gentle and kind in character or manner
senses.definition: kind, gentle and not easily angry in the way someone speaks or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 说话或行事和气、温和，不轻易发怒
senses.example: Her mild reply quietened the room more than any argument could.
senses.exampleCN: 她温和的回答比任何争辩都更能让房间安静下来。
senses.why: The oldest sense was moral: milde described a person who holds back anger, and that gentleness of character is still the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思带有道德色彩：milde 形容一个人压得住怒气；这种性情上的温和至今仍是这个词的中心。

senses.title: Warmer than expected for the season
senses.definition: used of weather or a climate that is not as cold or as harsh as it could be
senses.definitionCN: 用于天气或气候，表示没有本该有的那么冷、那么严酷
senses.example: The winter here is almost mild enough for the cat to sleep outdoors.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的冬天暖和得几乎能让猫睡在户外。
senses.why: Once the word means little force, it fits weather as well, because a mild winter is simply one that uses less of winter's force.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词表示「用力很小」，它也适用于天气：一个温和的冬天，就是冬天没怎么使出它的力气。

senses.title: Not strong in taste or effect
senses.definition: having a soft, not sharp taste, or a gentle effect on the body
senses.definitionCN: 味道柔和、不刺激，或对身体作用平缓
senses.example: The cheese is mild, so it suits people who dislike sharp flavours.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪味道清淡，适合不喜欢刺激口味的人。
senses.why: The same measure of low intensity transfers from pain to the tongue, so a mild cheese is one that hits the mouth with very little force.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「强度低」从疼痛转到舌头上：味道淡的奶酪，就是以很小的力气碰触口腔的那种。

intro.en: Mild goes back to Old English milde meaning gentle and merciful; it belongs to the Germanic branch and has no reliable Latin cognate.
intro.cn: mild 可追溯到古英语 milde，意为温和、仁慈；它属于日耳曼语这一支，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The adjective is generally traced to a Germanic form meaning gentle or kind, though its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个形容词来自日耳曼语中表示「温和、和善」的形式，但其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Milde meant gentle, merciful and kind, and it applied to rulers, judges and ordinary people alike.
items.cn: milde 意为温和、仁慈、和善，可用于君主、法官，也可用于普通人。

items.en: Middle English mild kept the moral sense of gentleness and began to describe weather and taste as well.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mild 保留「性情温和」的道德义，并开始形容天气与味道。

items.en: Writers extended mild from people to seasons, medicines and flavours, wherever force was noticeably low.
items.cn: 文人把 mild 从人扩展到季节、药物与味道，凡是用力明显较小之处都可以用它。

items.en: Modern English uses mild most often for small degrees of illness, gentle manners, soft weather and light flavours.
items.cn: 现代英语中，mild 最常用于轻微的病、和气的举止、温和的天气与清淡的味道。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on mild and one word that only shares its shape; the near-meaning group collects words for gentleness, slightness and softness.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 mild 上的词族，外加一个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收表示温和、轻微与柔软的词。

entries.definition: In a gentle way, or only a little.
entries.definitionCN: 以温和的方式，或只稍微地。

entries.definition: The quality of being gentle or not severe.
entries.definitionCN: 温和或不严重的性质。

entries.definition: A fungus that grows on damp surfaces; only the spelling is close and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 生长在潮湿表面的霉；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having a gentle way of behaving, built from mild and mannered.
entries.definitionCN: 举止温和的，由 mild 与 mannered 构成。

entries.definition: Soft and kind in manner, without force.
entries.definitionCN: 举止柔和、善意，不带强势。

entries.definition: Not hard or sharp, either to touch or to hear.
entries.definitionCN: 触感或听感上不硬、不刺。

entries.definition: Small in degree or amount, said of damage or change.
entries.definitionCN: 程度或数量小，用于损伤或变化。

entries.definition: Neither too much nor too little, kept within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 既不过多也不过少，保持在限度之内。

entries.definition: Mild and steady, especially of climate.
entries.definitionCN: 温和而稳定，尤指气候。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on an Old English adjective for gentleness; its family keeps returning to small force, soft weather and the kind of manner that holds anger back.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在一个意为温和的古英语形容词上，同族词反复回到「用力很小」、柔和的天气，以及压得住怒气的举止。

normal.en: Milde in Old English meant gentle and merciful, so mild begins as a moral word rather than a medical one.
normal.cn: 古英语 milde 意为温和、仁慈，所以 mild 起初属于道德词汇，而不是医学词汇。

normal.en: The word measures how little force is used, which is why a mild fever and a mild winter feel like the same idea.
normal.cn: 这个词衡量的是「用力有多小」，所以轻微发烧与温和的冬天感觉上是同一个想法。

normal.en: Milder and mildest add -er and -est, because mild is a short adjective that takes the regular comparison.
normal.cn: milder 与 mildest 分别加 -er 与 -est，因为 mild 是短形容词，走规则比较级。

normal.en: Mildly adds -ly and keeps the meaning of small force or gentle manner.
normal.cn: mildly 加 -ly，保留了「力气小」或「举止温和」的意思。

normal.en: Mildew looks close but means a mould; the two words only share a shape, not a source.
normal.cn: mildew 看上去很像，却指霉菌；两个词只共用外形，不共用来源。

abstract.en: A word for gentleness that also measures illness suggests that kindness and severity sit on one single scale.
abstract.cn: 一个既指温和又能衡量病情的词说明：善意与严重程度坐在同一把尺子上。

abstract.en: Mild weather is winter using less of its force, a picture that makes climate feel almost like a person holding back.
abstract.cn: 温和的天气就是冬天少用了些力气，这个画面让气候几乎像一个人收住了手。

abstract.en: Because mild can describe a voice, a fever and a cheese, the word quietly claims that force is what all three have in common.
abstract.cn: 因为 mild 能形容嗓音、发烧和奶酪，这个词其实在说：三者共通之处就是「力气的大小」。

examples.en: He had a mild fever and stayed home for one day.
examples.cn: 他发了低烧，在家待了一天。

examples.en: The winter here is almost mild enough for the cat to sleep outdoors.
examples.cn: 这里的冬天暖和得几乎能让猫睡在户外。

examples.en: The cheese is mild, so it suits people who dislike sharp flavours.
examples.cn: 这种奶酪味道清淡，适合不喜欢刺激口味的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迈尔德」——迈着慢步、脾气很软的人；记住 mild 是温和的、轻微的。

root: 古英语 milde（温和的、仁慈的）来自日耳曼语中表示「和善」的形式；一般认为其更早来源不确定，且没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is low force; the senses spread from a slight illness to a gentle manner, soft weather and a light taste.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「用力很小」；义项从轻微的病扩到和气的举止、柔和的天气与清淡的味道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a winter afternoon, sunlight falling across a yard, a cat stretching on the stone steps.
core.cn: 核心意象：冬日午后，阳光斜照进院子，一只猫在石阶上伸了个懒腰。

branches.en: a thermometer showing only a small rise
branches.cn: 温度计上只升了一小格

branches.en: a soft answer that ends an argument
branches.cn: 一句结束争吵的柔和回答

branches.en: a cat sleeping outside in midwinter
branches.cn: 隆冬里睡在户外的猫

branches.en: a pale cheese that does not bite the tongue
branches.cn: 一块不刺激舌头的浅色奶酪

branches.en: a nurse speaking softly about a small fever
branches.cn: 护士低声说着轻微的发热

intro.en: The word is carried by an Old English adjective of gentleness, its Middle English respelling, and English endings that build the adverb, the noun and the comparative.
intro.cn: 这个词由意为温和的古英语形容词、中古英语拼写，以及构成副词、名词与比较级的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mild: the word belongs to the Germanic branch, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: mild 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它属于日耳曼语这一支，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

definition_zh: 英里；很长的距离；很大的差距
definition_en: a unit of distance of about one and six tenths kilometres; a long distance in everyday speech; and a large amount or degree of difference, especially in the phrase by a mile
core_image: 公路旁的里程碑立在草丛里，石面被风雨磨得发白，远处还有下一块
scene: 公路沿着荒原一直伸到天边，草丛里立着一块被风雨磨白的路碑，司机盯着它数着还有多远。The next town is still a mile beyond the last bend.
sceneCN: 这里是「英里」（第 1 个义项：距离单位）；句意为过了最后一个弯，下一座镇子还有一英里的路。图中可辨识物件：草丛里的路碑、伸向天边的公路、远处的弯道。

pos.zh: 英里；很长的距离；很大差距

derivatives.zh: 由 mile 加 -age 构成，义为「里程；油耗」
由 mile 加 -er 构成，义为「一英里赛跑选手」
由 mile 与 stone 复合而成，义为「里程碑；重要节点」

senses.title: A unit of distance used in Britain and America
senses.definition: a unit of distance used mainly in the United States and Britain, equal to about one and six tenths kilometres
senses.definitionCN: 主要在美国和英国使用的距离单位，约合一点六公里
senses.example: The next town is still a mile beyond the last bend.
senses.exampleCN: 过了最后一个弯，下一座镇子还有一英里。
senses.why: The Latin phrase behind the word meant a thousand paces, so the mile began as a counted walk rather than an abstract length.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁短语意为「一千步」，所以英里最初是一段数出来的路，而不是一个抽象的长度。

senses.title: A long distance in everyday speech
senses.definition: a long way, used loosely in conversation rather than as an exact measurement
senses.definitionCN: 口语中泛指很远的距离，并不作为精确度量
senses.example: From the hill you can see the sea, though it looks miles away.
senses.exampleCN: 从山上能看见海，虽然它看上去远得很。
senses.why: Because a mile is a noticeable stretch of road, the plural easily becomes a loose word for any distance that feels long.
senses.whyCN: 因为一英里是一段能明显感觉到的路，复数形式便很容易变成泛指「任何觉得远」的距离。

senses.title: A large amount or degree of difference
senses.definition: a great amount or degree of difference, especially in the phrase by a mile
senses.definitionCN: 差距或程度很大，尤用于短语 by a mile
senses.example: Her second design was better by a mile.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第二个设计要好得多。
senses.why: A race decided by a mile is decided by a visible stretch of road, so the word turns physical distance into the size of any gap.
senses.whyCN: 以「一英里」之差决出的比赛，是靠一段看得见的路来分胜负；于是这个词把物理距离变成了任何差距的大小。

intro.en: Mile comes from a Latin phrase for a thousand paces, shortened in English to a single word for a measured stretch of road.
intro.cn: mile 来自拉丁语中表示「一千步」的短语，在英语里缩略成一个词，指一段被丈量过的路。

items.en: Mille was the Latin word for a thousand, and it stood at the head of the phrase that named the Roman mile.
items.cn: mille 是拉丁语中表示「一千」的词，也是罗马「里」这一说法开头的词。

items.en: The full phrase milia passuum meant a thousand double paces, the Roman unit for a long march.
items.cn: 完整的短语 milia passuum 意为「一千个双步」，是罗马人计量长途行军的单位。

items.en: Old English borrowed the shortened form as mil, a unit of distance used in land measurement and travel.
items.cn: 古英语借入缩短后的形式 mil，用作丈量土地与旅行中的距离单位。

items.en: Middle English mile kept the unit, but its exact length still varied from place to place.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mile 保留了这一单位，但它确切的长度在各地方仍有差异。

items.en: Modern English fixed the mile at a standard length and added loose uses such as 「miles away」 and 「by a mile」.
items.cn: 现代英语把英里的长度固定下来，并发展出「miles away」「by a mile」这类宽泛用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the mile family and one word that only shares its shape; the near-meaning group collects other units of distance and the general idea of distance.
note.cn: 形近组收 mile 的词族，外加一个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收其他距离单位以及「距离」这一总称。

entries.definition: Distance travelled, measured in miles, or the fuel used over that distance.
entries.definitionCN: 以英里计的行车距离，或这段距离的耗油量。

entries.definition: A stone marking a mile, later any important stage.
entries.definitionCN: 标明一英里的石标，后指任何重要阶段。

entries.definition: A runner or horse that races over one mile.
entries.definitionCN: 跑一英里距离的选手或马。

entries.definition: Only the shape and the sound are close; this word means to turn up the mouth in amusement, and its origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写与读音相近；这个词意为开心地扬起嘴角，词源不同。

entries.definition: A metric unit of distance, about five eighths of a mile.
entries.definitionCN: 公制距离单位，约合八分之五英里。

entries.definition: A unit of length equal to three feet.
entries.definitionCN: 等于三英尺的长度单位。

entries.definition: An old unit of distance, roughly three miles on land.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时的距离单位，陆上约合三英里。

entries.definition: The space between two points, without naming a unit.
entries.definitionCN: 两点之间的空间，不指定单位。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin phrase for a thousand paces; its family keeps returning to measured road, marked stones and the loose feeling of somewhere far.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「一千步」的短语上；同族词反复回到被丈量的路、立在路边的石标，以及「很远」这种宽泛的感觉。

normal.en: Mille in Latin means a thousand, and milia passuum was a thousand paces.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mille 意为一千，milia passuum 就是一千个步子。

normal.en: The Roman mile was a counted march, which is why the word feels like a stretch of road rather than a number.
normal.cn: 罗马的「里」是一段数出来的行军路程，所以这个词感觉像一段路，而不是一个数字。

normal.en: Old English shortened the phrase to mil, and English kept only the unit, not the thousand.
normal.cn: 古英语把短语缩短成 mil，英语只留下单位，丢掉了「一千」这层意思。

normal.en: Milestone joins mile to stone, a real stone set beside the road to mark each mile.
normal.cn: milestone 把 mile 与 stone 组合，指路边为标记每英里而立的真石头。

normal.en: 「Miles away」 and 「by a mile」 loosen the unit into a picture of any long distance or wide gap.
normal.cn: 「miles away」与「by a mile」把这个单位放宽成任何长距离或大差距的画面。

abstract.en: A unit built from a thousand steps suggests that early measurement was simply walking, counted and named.
abstract.cn: 一个由「一千步」构成的单位说明：早期的度量不过是走路，数出来，再给它一个名字。

abstract.en: When a fixed mile becomes miles away, a precise unit turns into a human feeling of distance.
abstract.cn: 当固定的 mile 变成 miles away，精确的单位就变成了人对距离的感受。

abstract.en: By a mile measures a gap in road lengths, a reminder that we often describe victory as travelling further.
abstract.cn: by a mile 用路的长度衡量差距，这提醒人：我们常把胜利说成「走得更远」。

examples.en: The next town is still a mile beyond the last bend.
examples.cn: 过了最后一个弯，下一座镇子还有一英里。

examples.en: From the hill you can see the sea, though it looks miles away.
examples.cn: 从山上能看见海，虽然它看上去远得很。

examples.en: Her second design was better by a mile.
examples.cn: 她的第二个设计要好得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迈尔」——迈开步子走很远，一英里一英里地数；记住 mile 是英里，也指很远。

root: 拉丁语 mille（一千）构成短语 milia passuum（一千步，即罗马里），缩略为古英语 mil，再演变为 mile；同族词多与里程、路标有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a counted march of a thousand paces; the senses divide into the fixed unit, the loose sense of a long way, and the size of a gap.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一段数以千步计的行军路程；义项分为固定的距离单位、泛指「很远」，以及差距的大小。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mile marker standing in the grass, its face worn pale by wind and rain, with another stone visible further on.
core.cn: 核心意象：公路旁的里程碑立在草丛里，石面被风雨磨白，远处还有下一块。

branches.en: a stone marker half hidden in grass
branches.cn: 半掩在草丛里的石标

branches.en: a driver counting markers along a straight road
branches.cn: 司机沿直路数着一块块路标

branches.en: a sea that looks tiny from a hilltop
branches.cn: 山顶上显得很小的海

branches.en: two designs laid side by side, one clearly ahead
branches.cn: 并排的两份设计，一份明显领先

branches.en: a finish line crossed with room to spare
branches.cn: 拉开很大余量冲过的终点线

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin numeral for a thousand, the distance phrase built on it, the Old English shortened form, and English endings that build the mileage and landmark words.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示「一千」的数词、由它构成的距离短语、古英语的缩略形式，以及构成里程与路标词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 军事的；军队的；军用的；军人式的；军队；军方
definition_en: relating to soldiers, armed forces, or war; also, as a noun, the armed forces of a country taken as one body
core_image: 一队士兵踏着同一节奏行进，枪挎在肩，靴底压过碎石
scene: 天刚亮，一队士兵沿着山口悄悄行进，靴底踩得碎石作响。At dawn the military column moved through the pass without a sound, rifles slung and boots crunching on the gravel.
sceneCN: 这里 military 是「军事的、军队的」（第 1 个义项：属于军队或战争的）；句意：黎明时分，这支军队的队伍悄无声息地穿过山口，枪挎在肩上，靴子踩得碎石作响。场景要点：天刚亮、狭窄山口、成列行进的士兵、肩上的步枪、碎石上传来的靴声；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 军事的；军队的；军用的；军人式的
军队；军方（与定冠词连用，the military）

collocations.zh: 军队；军方（作为一个整体）

derivatives.zh: 军国主义；尚武精神
军国主义者；军事迷
军国主义的；黩武的
使军事化；使军队化
军事化
在军事上；以军事手段

senses.title: Of soldiers and war
senses.definition: relating to soldiers, armies, or the conduct of war in general
senses.definitionCN: 与士兵、军队或战争行为有关的
senses.example: The museum's new wing is devoted to military history.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的新展区专门展示军事史。
senses.why: Latin militaris was simply the adjective of miles, 'soldier'. Anything it described belonged to the soldier's world, and that broad belonging is still the first sense in English.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 militaris 就是 miles（士兵）的形容词。它修饰的任何东西都属于士兵的世界，这种宽泛的归属至今仍是英语里的第一个义项。

senses.title: Done by soldiers, for soldiers
senses.titleCN: 由军人执行、供军队使用
senses.definition: carried out by soldiers or intended for the armed forces, rather than merely discussing them
senses.definitionCN: 由军人执行或供武装部队使用的，而不只是谈论军队
senses.example: The old airfield is now used for military training.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧机场现在用于军事训练。
senses.why: The adjective does not only label a topic; it also marks who acts and who benefits. A military operation is planned and run by soldiers, so the word moves from 'about soldiers' to 'by and for soldiers'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词不只标注话题，还标明谁在行动、谁在受益。军事行动由军人筹划和执行，于是这个词从“关于士兵”走到“由士兵做、为士兵做”。

senses.title: Soldier-like precision
senses.definition: used figuratively of behaviour that is as exact, orderly, and disciplined as a soldier's
senses.definitionCN: 比喻像军人一样精确、整齐、守纪律的行为
senses.example: She folded the map with military precision and handed it back.
senses.exampleCN: 她以军人般的精确折好地图，递了回去。
senses.why: Soldiers drill until every movement is measured and repeated. The adjective borrows that drilled exactness and lends it to civilian actions that have nothing to do with armies.
senses.whyCN: 士兵反复操练，直到每个动作都被量得准确、重复得整齐。这个形容词借来那种操练出来的精确，借给与军队无关的日常动作。

senses.title: By force, not by talk
senses.definition: describing a solution or spirit that relies on armed force or favours it
senses.definitionCN: 形容依靠武力或崇尚武力的解决办法与精神
senses.example: The dispute was settled by military means after talks failed.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判失败后，这场争端以军事手段解决。
senses.why: If the soldier's instrument is force, then calling a solution military announces that force will be used. The adjective shifts from describing an institution to recommending its method.
senses.whyCN: 如果士兵的工具是武力，那么把一个解决办法称为军事的，就是在宣告将动用武力。这个形容词从描述一种机构，转为推荐它的手段。

senses.title: The whole body of soldiers
senses.definition: with the definite article, the armed forces of a country considered as one collective body
senses.definitionCN: 与定冠词连用，指一国的武装力量整体
senses.example: The military were called in to clear the roads after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，军队被调来清理道路。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by taking 'the': the military, short for the military forces. A collective noun names all the soldiers as one thing, just as the column in the core image moves as one body.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词加上定冠词就变成了名词：“the military”，是“the military forces”的省略。集合名词把所有士兵命名成一个东西，正如核心意象里的队伍作为一个整体移动。

senses.title: The military as a power bloc
senses.titleCN: 军方：作为政治权力机构
senses.definition: the armed forces viewed as an institution that can act in politics and hold power
senses.definitionCN: 把武装部队看作能够在政治中行动、掌握权力的机构
senses.example: The military seized power overnight and closed the parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 军方一夜之间夺取政权，并关闭了议会。
senses.why: Once the column of soldiers acts as a single actor in public life, 'the military' stops meaning a crowd of men and starts meaning an institution with its own will and weight.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这支队伍在公共生活中作为一个单一行动者行事，the military 就不再指一群士兵，而开始指一个有自己的意志与分量的机构。

senses.title: One soldier, old-fashioned
senses.definition: in older usage, a soldier or a military man, countable and now rare
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指一名军人或军事人员，可数，现已罕见
senses.example: The old novel describes a retired officer simply as 'a military'.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧小说把一名退役军官径称为“一名军人”。
senses.why: The noun first named one person, 'a military man' (1736), before it named the whole body. The singular use survives only as an archaism, a fossil of the earlier step.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词先指一个人，即“a military man”（1736 年），后来才指整个群体。单数用法只作为古语残存下来，是较早那一步的化石。

senses.title: Service in the ranks
senses.definition: in phrases such as 'in the military', the state or career of serving in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 在“in the military”一类短语中，指在武装部队中服役的状态或经历
senses.example: He spent six years in the military before returning to the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他服役六年，之后回到农场。
senses.why: To be in the military is to stand inside that collective body. The core image of a formed column becomes a place a person can enter, belong to, and leave.
senses.whyCN: 身处军队，就是站进那个集体之中。核心意象里列队成形的队伍，变成了一个人可以进入、归属并离开的地方。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: used attributively to name an academic field whose subject is armies, wars, and defence
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，命名以军队、战争与防务为对象的学科领域
senses.example: She teaches military history at the war college.
senses.exampleCN: 她在军事学院教授军事史。
senses.why: The same adjective that marks soldiers' business can mark the study of that business. The object of the field is still the column, only now it is observed from a desk instead of a trench.
senses.whyCN: 标记士兵事务的同一个形容词，也可以标记对这一事务的研究。这个领域的对象仍是那支队伍，只是现在是从书桌前观察，而不是从战壕里。

intro.en: Military is a Latin adjective that English borrowed through French in the fifteenth century; the collective noun arrived three centuries later, and the origin of the Latin base is still unsettled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: military 是 15 世纪经法语借入英语的拉丁语形容词；集合名词要晚三百年才出现，而拉丁语词根的来历至今没有定论。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as militari, 'pertaining to or befitting soldiers; used, done, or brought about by soldiers'. It came from Old French militaire (14c.) and directly from Latin militaris.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为 militari，意为“与士兵有关或适合士兵的；由士兵使用、完成或造成的”。它来自古法语 militaire（14 世纪），并直接来自拉丁语 militaris。

items.en: Latin militaris meant 'of soldiers or war, of military service, warlike'. It was formed from miles (genitive militis), 'soldier', a word of unknown origin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 militaris 意为“士兵的、战争的、兵役的、尚武的”。它由 miles（属格 militis）“士兵”构成，而这个词的来历不明。

items.en: The origin of miles is unsettled. It may be Etruscan, or it may mean 'one who marches in a troop', which would connect it to Sanskrit melah 'assembly' and Greek homilos 'assembled crowd'. De Vaan finds it tempting to link it to milia 'thousands', hence *mili-it- 'who goes with the thousand'. None of these is proved.
items.cn: miles 的来历没有定论。它可能来自伊特鲁里亚语，也可能意为“随队伍行进的人”，从而与梵语 melah“集会”、希腊语 homilos“聚集的人群”相联系。De Vaan 认为把它与 milia“数千”联系起来很诱人，即 *mili-it-“随千人同行的人”。这些说法都未被证明。

items.en: The noun first meant 'a military man' (1736). 'Soldiers generally' is recorded from 1757, and it is commonly used only with the definite article.
items.cn: 名词最初意为“军人”（1736）。泛指“士兵、军队”的用法记录于 1757 年，而且通常只与定冠词连用。

items.en: The adjective spreads into fixed phrases: military age, the age at which one becomes liable for service (1737); military police (1827); and military-industrial complex, coined in Eisenhower's farewell speech (1961).
items.cn: 这个形容词扩散到固定短语中：military age 指应服兵役的年龄（1737）；military police 即军事警察（1827）；military-industrial complex 即军工复合体，由艾森豪威尔在告别演说中铸成（1961）。

items.en: Militia is a separate borrowing: 1580s, 'system of military discipline', from Latin militia 'military service', and only from the 1690s 'citizen army'. Militarism (1841) came from French militarisme. Military is the adjective, militia the citizen body, militarism the ideology.
items.cn: militia 是另一次借入：16 世纪 80 年代指“军事训练制度”，来自拉丁语 militia“兵役”，到 17 世纪 90 年代才指“公民军队”。militarism（1841）来自法语 militarisme。military 是形容词，militia 是公民武装，militarism 是主义。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin miles stem but has drifted into different jobs; the second compares the ordinary words for organized fighters.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语 miles 词干，却各自漂向不同的职责；第二组比较表示有组织武装人员的常用词。

entries.definition: a body of citizens enrolled for military service in an emergency, not professional soldiers. It is a force, while military is the adjective of the professional institution.
entries.definitionCN: 紧急时征召服役的公民队伍，不是职业军人。它是一支力量，而 military 是职业军队的形容词。

entries.definition: willing to use strong or violent action for a cause, or a person who is. It describes a stance or a person, never an army as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意为某项事业采取强硬或暴力行动的，或指这样的人。它描述一种立场或一个人，从不指整支军队。

entries.definition: the belief that a country should keep a strong military and use it aggressively. It names a doctrine, not the forces themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 认为国家应保持强大军力并积极使用武力的信念。它命名一种主义，而不是军队本身。

entries.definition: organized and armed like an army but outside the official armed forces. The prefix para- 'beside' marks the difference from regular military bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 组织与武装像军队、却处于正规武装力量之外的。前缀 para-“在旁”标出它与正规军事组织的区别。

entries.definition: the branch of a country's forces that fights on land, or a large body of soldiers. It is one service, while the military can mean all services together.
entries.definitionCN: 一国武装力量中在陆地作战的分支，或一大群士兵。它是一个军种，而 the military 可指所有军种的整体。

entries.definition: the combined military forces of a country, including army, navy, and air force. It is the full official phrase for what 'the military' names in one word.
entries.definitionCN: 一国武装力量的总和，包括陆军、海军与空军。它是对 the military 一词所指对象的完整正式说法。

entries.definition: soldiers, especially those serving in a particular place or operation. It counts people, while the military names an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 士兵，尤指在某一地点或行动中服役的人。它数的是人，而 the military 命名的是一种机构。

entries.definition: organized groups of soldiers, often qualified as land, air, or naval forces. It is a flexible plural, close to 'the military' but usually needs a qualifier.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的军人群体，常以陆地、空中或海上限定。它是灵活的复数，接近 the military，但通常需要限定语。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin miles 'soldier', its adjective militaris, the -ary ending, and the separate but related borrowings militia and militarism.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 miles“士兵”、它的形容词 militaris、后缀 -ary，以及另行借入但相关的 militia 与 militarism。

normal.en: miles is Latin for 'soldier'; militaris is its adjective. Military begins as nothing more than 'of the soldier'.
normal.cn: miles 是拉丁语的“士兵”，militaris 是它的形容词。military 最初不过是“士兵的”。

normal.en: The adjective came first, in the fifteenth century; the noun 'the military' for soldiers as a body is recorded only in 1757.
normal.cn: 形容词先出现，在 15 世纪；把士兵作为整体来称的 the military 直到 1757 年才有记录。

normal.en: The -ary ending makes an adjective, so military, militarily, militarism and militarize all grow from the same stem with different endings.
normal.cn: -ary 结尾使它成为形容词，所以 military、militarily、militarism、militarize 都从同一词干加上不同词尾长出来。

normal.en: militia is a separate borrowing from Latin militia 'military service'; its 'citizen army' sense is only from the 1690s.
normal.cn: militia 是从拉丁语 militia“兵役”另行借入的词；它的“公民军队”义要到 17 世纪 90 年代才出现。

normal.en: The definite article matters: the military is the whole body, while a military is an old-fashioned way to say one soldier.
normal.cn: 定冠词很关键：the military 指整个军队，而 a military 是旧式说法，指一名军人。

abstract.en: Picture a column of boots striking gravel at the same instant. The sound is not many sounds but one sound repeated, and that is what makes it military.
abstract.cn: 想象一列靴子在同一瞬间踏在碎石上。那声音不是许多声音，而是一个声音的重复，正是这种重复使它成为“军事的”。

abstract.en: The adjective is a uniform that can be put on anything: a bridge, a budget, a history, a way of folding a map.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词是一套可以套在任何东西上的制服：一座桥、一份预算、一段历史、一种折地图的方式。

abstract.en: When the column stops marching and starts deciding, it becomes 'the military' — one actor with a will, not a crowd of men.
abstract.cn: 当这支队伍停止行进、开始作决定，它就变成了“军方”——一个有意愿的行动者，而不是一群士兵。

examples.en: Military spending rose for the third year in a row.
examples.cn: 军费开支连续第三年上升。

examples.en: The airfield is still under military control, and no civilian flights are allowed.
examples.cn: 这座机场仍处于军事管制之下，不允许民用航班起降。

examples.en: After the earthquake, the military was sent in to reopen the mountain roads.
examples.cn: 地震之后，军队被派去重新打通山路。

root: 源自拉丁语 miles“士兵”的形容词 militaris，核心是“属于士兵与军队的”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of military, all growing from one picture: a body of soldiers moving as a single column, and then acting as a single institution.
sensesIntro.cn: military 的九个义项都长自同一幅画面：一队士兵作为一个整体行进，随后作为一个整体机构行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of soldiers stepping as one body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队士兵作为一个整体迈步。

branches.en: SOLDIER'S WORLD: the adjective first marks what belongs to soldiers, then what is done by them and for them.
branches.cn: 士兵的世界：这个形容词先标记属于士兵的东西，再标记由士兵做、为士兵做的事。

branches.en: BORROWED QUALITIES: drilled exactness is lent to civilian actions, and the soldier's instrument, force, is lent to solutions.
branches.cn: 借来的品质：操练出的精确被借给日常动作，士兵的工具即武力被借给解决办法。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND POLITICAL: 'the military' first names all soldiers as one body, then names that body as a power in politics.
branches.cn: 集体与政治：the military 先把所有士兵命名成一个整体，再把这个整体命名为政治中的一种权力。

branches.en: ONE MAN AND A CAREER: the old singular names a single soldier, while 'in the military' names service inside the body.
branches.cn: 个人与职业：旧式单数指一名军人，而 in the military 指在这个整体内部服役。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the same adjective marks the academic field that observes armies from a desk.
branches.cn: 研究领域：同一个形容词标记从书桌前观察军队的学科。

intro.en: Military is a Latin adjective ending in -ary; the stem milit- also carries -ia, -ism, -ist, -istic, -ize and -ation into English. The prefix para- in paramilitary is Greek, added later.
intro.cn: military 是带 -ary 后缀的拉丁语形容词；词干 milit- 还把 -ia、-ism、-ist、-istic、-ize 与 -ation 带进英语。paramilitary 里的前缀 para- 是后来加上的希腊语成分。

latinIntro.en: Three Latin words sit behind the family: miles 'soldier', its adjective militaris, and militia 'military service'. The origin of miles itself is disputed, so no deeper root can be stated as fact.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族背后有三个拉丁词：miles“士兵”、它的形容词 militaris，以及 militia“兵役”。miles 本身的来历有争议，因此不能把更深的词根当作事实来陈述。

items.meaningCN: 士兵的；战争的（milit- 士兵 + -ary 形容词后缀）
items.example: The country keeps a large military budget.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家维持着庞大的军事预算。

items.meaning: the belief in strong armed forces and their use
items.meaningCN: 军国主义；尚武精神（-ism 构成主义）
items.example: The book traces the rise of militarism before the war.
items.exampleCN: 这本书追溯了战前军国主义的兴起。

items.example: The general was widely seen as a militarist.
items.exampleCN: 这位将军被普遍看作军国主义者。

items.meaningCN: 军国主义的；黩武的（-ic 构成形容词）

items.exampleCN: 这场阅兵带有强烈的黩武色彩。

items.meaningCN: 使军事化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The island was militarized during the crisis.
items.exampleCN: 危机期间，这座岛屿被军事化了。

items.meaningCN: 军事化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: People protested against the militarization of the police.
items.exampleCN: 人们抗议警察的军事化。

items.meaning: a citizen army called out in an emergency
items.meaningCN: 民兵组织；紧急时征召的公民武装（拉丁语“兵役”）
items.example: The local militia guarded the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 当地民兵守卫着那座桥。

items.meaningCN: 好战的；激进分子（-ant 构成形容词或指人）
items.example: A militant wing of the movement rejected the talks.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动的激进一派拒绝了谈判。

items.meaning: to work against something, as evidence or circumstance
items.meaningCN: 妨碍；起不利作用（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The high cost militates against any quick repair.
items.exampleCN: 高昂的成本不利于任何快速修复。

items.meaning: armed like an army but outside it
items.meaningCN: 准军事的（para- 在旁 + military 军事的）
items.example: A paramilitary group controlled the border road.
items.exampleCN: 一个准军事组织控制着那条边境公路。

senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指的是磨石，所以第一层含义就是围绕那块磨石建起来的地方。

senses.title: A factory fitted with machinery
senses.definition: a factory in which a particular material or product is made by machinery, such as steel or paper
senses.definitionCN: 用机械制造某种材料或产品的工厂，如钢厂或造纸厂
senses.example: The steel mill kept three shifts running through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家钢厂整个冬天三班不停。
senses.why: Once a mill is a building full of turning machinery, the word widens from grinding grain to making any product on a large scale.
senses.whyCN: 既然磨坊是一座装满转动机械的建筑，这个词就从磨谷子扩展到大规模制造任何产品。

senses.title: A small machine for grinding
senses.definition: a small device with blades or stones that grinds a food or material inside it
senses.definitionCN: 内置刀片或石磨、用来磨碎食物或材料的小器具
senses.example: She gave the pepper mill three quick turns over the pan.
senses.exampleCN: 她在锅上把胡椒研磨器快速转了三下。
senses.why: The stone that does the grinding can be shrunk into a hand tool, and the tool inherits the name of the whole building.
senses.whyCN: 负责研磨的那块石头可以缩小成一件手持工具，而工具继承了整座建筑的名字。

senses.title: To grind something into powder or a soft mass
senses.definition: to break a solid substance into powder or a smooth mass by crushing it between hard surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 把固体在硬面之间压碎，使其变成粉末或柔滑的团块
senses.example: The workers mill the grain between two heavy stones.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们用两块重石把谷物磨碎。
senses.why: The verb simply puts the building's action into a word: to mill is to do what the mill does to grain.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把磨坊的动作写成一个词：to mill 就是做磨坊对谷物所做的事。

senses.title: Of a crowd, to move about without a clear aim
senses.definition: of a group of people or animals, to move around in a confused, purposeless way
senses.definitionCN: 指一群人或动物毫无目的地、混乱地来回走动
senses.example: Fans milled around the gate long after the concert ended.
senses.exampleCN: 演唱会散场很久了，歌迷们还在大门附近打转。
senses.why: The turning of the mill wheel supplies the picture: people circling with no direction look like something being turned round and round.
senses.whyCN: 磨坊水轮的转动提供了这个画面：没有方向地绕圈的人，看上去就像被转来转去的东西。

intro.en: Mill comes from Late Latin molina, a word for a mill built on Latin mola, a millstone, and molere, to grind; English took the word through Germanic channels.
intro.cn: mill 来自晚期拉丁语 molina（磨坊），其基础是拉丁语 mola（磨石）与 molere（磨），再经日耳曼语转借进入英语。

items.en: Mola meant a millstone, the hard stone on which grain was rubbed or crushed.
items.cn: mola 意为磨石，即用来摩擦、压碎谷物的硬石。

items.en: Molere was the verb to grind, and it stands behind the whole family of milling words.
items.cn: molere 是动词「磨」，整套与研磨有关的词都由它而来。

items.en: Late Latin molina named a mill, was derived from mola, and was passed on to the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的 molina 指磨坊，由 mola 派生而来，并传给了日耳曼诸语。

items.en: Old English borrowed the word as mylen or myl, meaning a mill for grinding grain.
items.cn: 古英语借入这个词，写作 mylen 或 myl，指磨谷子的磨坊。

items.en: Modern English shortened the form to mill and widened it from grain to factories, small grinders and the aimless circling of a crowd.
items.cn: 现代英语把它缩短为 mill，并从谷物扩展到工厂、小型研磨器，以及人群无功的打转。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the mill family and one word that only shares its shape; the near-meaning group collects words for factories and for grinding.
note.cn: 形近组收 mill 的词族，外加一个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收表示工厂与研磨的词。

entries.definition: A person who owns or works in a mill, from mill plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 经营或在磨坊工作的人，由 mill 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The act or process of grinding something in a mill.
entries.definitionCN: 在磨坊中研磨某物的动作或过程。

entries.definition: One of the heavy stones used for grinding grain; also used of a burden.
entries.definitionCN: 用于磨谷的重石之一；也比喻沉重负担。

entries.definition: Only the spelling and the vowel pattern are close; this word means a unit of distance, and its origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写与元音组合相近；这个词指距离单位，词源不同。

entries.definition: A building where goods are made in large quantities by machines.
entries.definitionCN: 用机器大批量制造商品的场所。

entries.definition: An industrial site with buildings and machinery for manufacturing.
entries.definitionCN: 带有厂房与机械的工业生产场所。

entries.definition: To crush something into small pieces or powder between hard surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 在硬面之间把东西压碎成小块或粉末。

entries.definition: A room or building where making or repairing is done, usually on a small scale.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或修理的房间或建筑，通常规模较小。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin millstone and its verb for grinding; the family keeps returning to the stone, the building around it, the factories it grew into and the wheel that turns.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语的磨石与「磨」这一动词上；同族词反复回到石头、围绕石头建起的建筑、由它长成的工厂，以及转动的轮子。

normal.en: Mola in Latin meant a millstone, so a mill is first of all a place built around a stone that grinds.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mola 意为磨石，所以 mill 首先是一个围绕磨石建起来的地方。

normal.en: Molere was to grind, and it links mill to a whole family of words about crushing and powder.
normal.cn: molere 意为磨，它把 mill 与一整族关于压碎与粉末的词连在一起。

normal.en: Mylen was the Old English borrowing, and the modern form cut it down to the single syllable mill.
normal.cn: mylen 是古英语借入的形式，现代形式把它缩成单音节的 mill。

normal.en: Miller adds -er and names the person who runs the mill, while milling names the work itself.
normal.cn: miller 加 -er 指经营磨坊的人，milling 则指这项工作本身。

normal.en: Mill around borrows the turning wheel: a crowd with no aim circles like something being ground.
normal.cn: mill around 借用了转动的轮子：没有目标的人群像被研磨的东西一样打转。

abstract.en: A word that means both a flour mill and a steel mill shows how one machine picture can cover every industry that turns raw material into something else.
abstract.cn: 一个既指面粉磨坊又指钢厂的词说明：同一幅机器画面能覆盖所有把原料变成别物的行业。

abstract.en: Mill around makes people into grain, moving in circles because nobody has set a direction.
abstract.cn: mill around 把人变成谷物，因为没有谁定下方向，只能绕圈。

abstract.en: Grinding is slow, heavy and repeated, which may be why the word also carries the sense of a long, hard process.
abstract.cn: 研磨缓慢、沉重而反复，这或许就是这个词也带着「漫长艰苦过程」意味的原因。

examples.en: The old mill has ground wheat for the village since before anyone can remember.
examples.cn: 这座老磨坊为村子磨麦子，久到没人记得是从何时开始。

examples.en: The steel mill kept three shifts running through the winter.
examples.cn: 这家钢厂整个冬天三班不停。

examples.en: Fans milled around the gate long after the concert ended.
examples.cn: 演唱会散场很久了，歌迷们还在大门附近打转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米了」——稻米进了磨坊，出来就成了米粉；记住 mill 是磨坊、磨碎。

root: 拉丁语 mola（磨石）与 molere（磨）组成晚期拉丁语 molina（磨坊），经日耳曼语转借为古英语 mylen，后缩为 mill；同族词多与研磨、工厂有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a stone that grinds; the senses spread from the mill building to the factory, the small grinder, the act of grinding and the aimless circling of a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块负责研磨的石头；义项从磨坊建筑扩到工厂、小型研磨器、磨碎的动作，以及人群无功的打转。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old mill by a river, its wooden wheel turned by water, fine flour flowing out of the stone channel.
core.cn: 核心意象：河边的老磨坊，木轮被水推着转，石磨里流出细细的面粉。

branches.en: a water wheel turning beside a stone wall
branches.cn: 水边转动的木轮与石墙

branches.en: a long shed roofed in steel beside a rail line
branches.cn: 铁轨旁一排钢顶厂房

branches.en: a small grinder on a kitchen table
branches.cn: 厨房桌上的一只小研磨器

branches.en: flour falling in a slow white line
branches.cn: 缓缓落下的一线白面粉

branches.en: a crowd circling a locked gate
branches.cn: 在锁着的大门前打转的人群

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin noun for a millstone, the verb to grind, the Late Latin name for a mill, the Old English borrowing and two English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语的磨石名词、表示「磨」的动词、晚期拉丁语的磨坊名、古英语借词，以及两个英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 毫克（千分之一克）；按毫克计的药量；极微的含量
definition_en: a unit of mass equal to one thousandth of a gram, and by extension a dose or a trace amount measured in that unit
core_image: 天平上一小撮白色粉末，指针几乎不动，刻度只轻轻跳了一格
scene: 药房里，穿白大褂的人把一片小药丸放到精密天平上，显示屏上的数字小得要用放大镜才看得清。The label says each tablet contains only a few milligrams of the active ingredient.
sceneCN: 这里是「毫克」（第 1 个义项：千分之一克的质量单位）；句意为标签标明每片药只含少量有效成分的毫克数。图中可辨识物件：白大褂、药丸、精密天平、被放大的显示屏。

derivatives.zh: 英式旧拼写，与 milligram 同义，仍见于较早的药品说明书
由希腊语 gramma 经法语 gramme 进入英语，义为「克」，是毫克所依据的基本单位
把前缀 milli- 换成 micro-（百万分之一），义为「微克」，比毫克再小一千倍

senses.title: One thousandth of a gram
senses.definition: a unit of mass in the metric system, equal to one thousandth of a gram
senses.definitionCN: 公制中量质量的一个单位，等于一克的千分之一
senses.example: The pharmacist weighed out four milligrams of the powder.
senses.exampleCN: 药剂师称出了四毫克粉末。
senses.why: The prefix milli- is Latin mille, a thousand, and gram is the base unit of mass; the name states its own size outright, one thousandth of a gram, so the unit sense is the arithmetic core the other senses grow from.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 milli- 来自拉丁语 mille（千），gram 是质量的基本单位，名字一拼起来就把大小说清楚了：一克的千分之一。所以「单位」这一层是整词的算术内核，其余用法都从这里往外长。

senses.title: A dose strength written in milligrams
senses.definition: the amount of a drug or nutrient stated in milligrams on a prescription, packet or label
senses.definitionCN: 处方、药盒或标签上用毫克标明的药物或营养成分含量
senses.example: The doctor lowered her daily dose by five milligrams.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把她的每日剂量减少了五毫克。
senses.why: A strong drug works in thousandths of a gram, so a prescription needs a unit fine enough to separate a helpful amount from a harmful one; the milligram became the natural word for the figure printed on the packet.
senses.whyCN: 强效药的有效量与危险量常常只差千分之几克，处方需要一个细到能分开「有用」和「有害」的单位，毫克于是成了药盒上那个数字的日常说法。

senses.title: A faint trace measured in the same unit
senses.definition: a very small quantity, counted in milligrams, found by careful testing in food, water or a sample
senses.definitionCN: 在食物、水或样品中经仔细检测才发现的极少量，以毫克计
senses.example: Testing found only milligrams of copper in the tap water.
senses.exampleCN: 检测发现自来水里只有几毫克铜。
senses.why: Minerals in food and water sit far below the scale of a gram, so labels and lab reports drop a thousandfold and count in milligrams; here the unit measures what a thing contains rather than what a person takes.
senses.whyCN: 食物和水里的矿物质远不到一克，标签与检验报告便下降一千倍、用毫克来点数；这时同一个单位量的是「某物里有什么」，而不是「一个人吃多少」。

intro.en: Milligram is a modern coinage of the metric system: a Latin prefix for a thousandth joined to a Greek word for a small weight, passed through French before it reached English.
intro.cn: milligram 是公制时代的近代造词：表示千分之一的拉丁前缀，接上希腊语中「小重量」的词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Mille was the Latin numeral for a thousand and gave the prefix milli-, which shrinks a unit to its thousandth.
items.cn: mille 是拉丁语的「千」，由此得到前缀 milli-，把一个单位缩小到它的千分之一。

items.en: Greek gramma first meant a written mark and later a small weight; French took it as gramme, the base unit of mass.
items.cn: 希腊语 gramma 最初指写下的记号，后来指小重量；法语取作 gramme，作为质量的基本单位。

items.en: French scientists coined milligramme while the metric system was being built in the late eighteenth century, joining milli- directly to gramme.
items.cn: 十八世纪末建立公制时，法国学者把 milli- 直接拼到 gramme 上，造出 milligramme。

items.en: English adopted the word as milligram in the nineteenth century, as metric measures spread through pharmacies, laboratories and trade.
items.cn: 十九世纪，随着公制进入药房、实验室与贸易，英语把这个词收作 milligram。

items.en: Modern usage keeps milligram for prescriptions, food labels and trace reports, where thousandths of a gram are ordinary working figures.
items.cn: 现代用法把 milligram 留在处方、食品标签与痕量报告里，千分之一克在那里是寻常的工作数字。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers spellings and units built on the same two building blocks; the near-meaning group gathers words for amounts and for old measures of mass.
note.cn: 形近组收由同样两个构件拼成的拼写与单位；近义组收表示「量」以及旧式质量单位的词。

entries.definition: An older British spelling of the same unit, still met in dated medical texts.
entries.definitionCN: 同一单位的英式旧拼写，仍见于较早的医学文本。

entries.definition: The base metric unit of mass, one thousand times larger than a milligram.
entries.definitionCN: 公制质量的基本单位，比毫克大一千倍。

entries.definition: A unit one thousandth of a milligram, used for vitamins and hormones.
entries.definitionCN: 比毫克再小一千倍的单位，用于维生素与激素。

entries.definition: A unit of volume built with the same milli- prefix, so it measures space rather than mass.
entries.definitionCN: 同用 milli- 前缀的体积单位，量的是空间而不是质量。

entries.definition: The amount of a medicine taken at one time, often stated in milligrams.
entries.definitionCN: 一次服用的药量，常以毫克表示。

entries.definition: An amount so small that only careful measurement can show it.
entries.definitionCN: 小到只有仔细测量才能显现的量。

entries.definition: An old unit of mass still used for bullets and medicines, about sixty-five milligrams.
entries.definitionCN: 仍用于子弹与药物的旧质量单位，约合六十五毫克。

entries.definition: A larger everyday unit of mass, equal to about twenty-eight grams.
entries.definitionCN: 日常使用的较大质量单位，约合二十八克。

normalIntro.en: The word is assembled from a prefix that means a thousandth and a base unit, and its family keeps returning to small measured amounts.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示千分之一的前缀和一个基本单位拼成，同族词反复回到「被量出来的小量」。

normal.en: Milli- is Latin for a thousandth and gram is the base unit, so the word needs no story once the two parts are known.
normal.cn: milli- 表示千分之一，gram 是基本单位，认识这两块，词义就不必再讲故事。

normal.en: A gram is about the weight of a paper clip, so a milligram is that clip cut into a thousand slivers too small to see.
normal.cn: 一克大约是一枚回形针的重量，一毫克就是把它切成一千片看不见的细屑。

normal.en: Prescriptions print milligrams because the gap between help and harm in a strong drug is often a few thousandths of a gram.
normal.cn: 处方上印毫克，是因为强效药「有效」与「有害」之间常常只差几千分之一克。

normal.en: Food labels count iron, sodium and vitamins in milligrams, since a meal holds these minerals far below a gram.
normal.cn: 食品标签用毫克标注铁、钠与维生素，因为一顿饭里这些矿物质的量远不到一克。

normal.en: Microgram is the next step down, one thousandth of a milligram, built simply by swapping milli- for micro-.
normal.cn: microgram 再往下一级，是毫克的千分之一，构词上只是把 milli- 换成 micro-。

abstract.en: A unit too small to move a kitchen scale is the one that decides whether a medicine heals or harms.
abstract.cn: 一个在厨房秤上毫无反应的单位，却决定了药是救人还是伤人。

abstract.en: Figures that look like dust on a screen still carry the full weight of a decision about a human body.
abstract.cn: 屏幕上像灰尘一样的数字，仍背着关于一个人身体的整个决定。

abstract.en: The word names its own size, and that honesty is exactly what makes it trusted in a laboratory.
abstract.cn: 这个词把自己的大小写在名字里，这份坦白正是它在实验室里被信任的原因。

examples.en: The recipe calls for two milligrams of the colouring agent.
examples.cn: 配方要求加入两毫克着色剂。

examples.en: The daily dose was reduced to fifty milligrams.
examples.cn: 每日剂量被降到五十毫克。

examples.en: Only a milligram of the mineral remains in each litre.
examples.cn: 每升水里只剩下了一毫克这种矿物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米粒」——milli 听起来像「米粒」，一克分成一千份，每份小得像一粒米；记住 milligram 是毫克。

root: 拉丁语 mille（千）派生前缀 milli-（千分之一），接希腊语 gramma（小重量）经法语 gramme，合成法语 milligramme，十九世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The arithmetic unit comes first; the other senses take that same tiny scale to the pharmacy counter and then to the food label and the water report.
sensesIntro.cn: 先立住那个算术意义上的单位；其余义项把同一把极小的尺子带到药房柜台，再带到食品标签与水质报告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pinch of white powder on a balance, the needle barely stirring as it moves one notch.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上一小撮白色粉末，指针只轻轻挪动一格。

branches.en: a balance needle moving one notch for a pinch of powder
branches.cn: 天平为一小撮粉末只挪动一格

branches.en: a prescription printed in figures smaller than a grain of salt
branches.cn: 处方上印着比盐粒还小的数字

branches.en: a nurse halving a tablet to shave off a few milligrams
branches.cn: 护士把药片对半切，削去几毫克

branches.en: a nutrition label read through a magnifying glass
branches.cn: 隔着放大镜读营养成分表

branches.en: a water report naming a metal found in traces
branches.cn: 水质报告里标出一种含量极微的金属

intro.en: The word stands on a Latin numeral for a thousand, a Greek word for a small weight, their French combination, and English endings that name the unit and its smaller relatives.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「千」的数词、希腊语表示「小重量」的词、二者在法语里的组合，以及命名单位与其更小同类的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the numeral for a thousand and the ordinal for a thousandth, the two forms that make the metric prefix possible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示「千」的数词与表示「第一千」的序数词，正是这两个形式使公制前缀得以成立。

definition_en: the number one million, and by extension an indefinitely large number or a fortune of that size

senses.title: The number one million
senses.definition: the exact number that equals one thousand thousands, written as a one followed by six zeros
senses.definitionCN: 精确等于一千个一千的数，写出来是一个后面跟六个零的数字
senses.example: The stadium holds a million people on a match day.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛日这座体育场能容纳一百万人。
senses.why: Mille in Latin means a thousand, and Italian added the augmentative suffix -one to produce a big thousand; the word was coined to name a sum that early speakers could barely count to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mille 是「千」，意大利语又加上增大后缀 -one，造出一个「大一号的千」；这个词被造出来，正是为了命名一个早期使用者几乎数不到的数目。

senses.title: A very great but uncounted number
senses.definition: an indefinitely large number of people or things, used when the exact count does not matter
senses.definitionCN: 数不清的大量人或物，用于说不上具体数目的时候
senses.example: Millions of birds cross this coast every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天都有数以百万计的鸟飞越这片海岸。
senses.why: Once the word pins down one exact million, it can also be loosened to mean any crowd past counting, because the number itself already sits at the edge of what a person can picture.
senses.whyCN: 当 million 先钉住一个精确的数，它也可以松开来指任何数不清的一大群，因为这个数本身就站在人还能想象的范围边缘。

senses.title: A fortune of that size
senses.definition: a very large amount of money, especially when spoken of as the goal or the price of something
senses.definitionCN: 一笔很大的钱，尤指被当作目标或代价谈起的时候
senses.example: He made his millions in shipping and gave much of it away.
senses.exampleCN: 他在航运业赚得巨额财富，又把其中许多捐了出去。
senses.why: A million pounds or dollars is the smallest sum that sounds like freedom, so the noun slid from the number to the fortune it stands for, and the plural carries that sense most easily.
senses.whyCN: 一百万镑或一百万美元，是最像一个「自由」门槛的数目，于是这个名词从数字滑向它所代表的财产，复数形式最容易带上这层意思。

intro.en: Million is a Romance coinage: a Latin thousand took an Italian suffix that made it mean a big thousand, then passed through French into English.
intro.cn: million 是罗曼语系的造词：拉丁语的「千」加上一个意大利语后缀，变成「大一号的千」，再经法语进入英语。

items.en: Mille was the Latin word for a thousand and the source of the whole family of million words.
items.cn: mille 是拉丁语里的「千」，也是整族 million 词的源头。

items.en: The neuter plural millia meant thousands and supplied the pattern for naming a very large counted mass.
items.cn: 中性复数 millia 意为「数以千计」，为命名极大的计数群体提供了样式。

items.en: Italian speakers are generally credited with coining milioni in the thirteenth century by adding the augmentative suffix -one to mille, so that a million was literally a big thousand.
items.cn: 一般认为，意大利语在十三世纪把增大后缀 -one 加到 mille 上造出 milioni，「百万」字面上就是一个「大一号的千」。

items.en: French took the Italian word as million and used it in accounts and records before passing it on to English.
items.cn: 法语把意大利语词取作 million，先在账目与记录里使用，再传给英语。

items.en: English million first named the exact number, then stretched into millions of and a million to one, all built on the idea of a crowd too big to count.
items.cn: 英语的 million 先指精确的数，后来伸展出「数以百万计」「百万分之一」等说法，都建立在「大到数不清」这个念头上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the words built on the same Latin thousand and the same Italian suffix; the near-meaning group gathers the number words above and below it on the same scale.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一个拉丁语「千」和同一个意大利语后缀构成的词；近义组收同一把数轴上比它高和比它低的数词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin thousand wearing an Italian augmentative suffix, and its family keeps climbing the same numerical ladder in bigger steps.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个披着意大利语增大后缀的拉丁语「千」，同族词反复在同一架数字梯子上迈更大的步子。

normal.en: Mille is Latin for a thousand, and the Italian suffix -one made it a big thousand before English borrowed the word.
normal.cn: mille 是拉丁语的「千」，意大利语后缀 -one 把它变成「大一号的千」，英语才借过来。

normal.en: The plural millia is why English can say millions, a word for an uncountable crowd as much as for a number.
normal.cn: 复数 millia 是英语能说 millions 的由来，这个词既指数不清的人群，也指一个数。

normal.en: Millionaire adds -aire, the French ending for a person, directly to the fortune itself.
normal.cn: millionaire 把法语里表示人的后缀 -aire 直接加在那笔财产后面。

normal.en: Millionth adds -th, the same ending that turns four into fourth, so the ordinal is ordinary English building, not a new root.
normal.cn: millionth 加的是把 four 变成 fourth 的那个 -th，属于寻常的英语构词，不是新词根。

normal.en: One in a million works because the number is already the edge of the imaginable, so a single case inside it feels miraculous.
normal.cn: one in a million 之所以成立，是因为这个数已到想象的边缘，混在其中的单独一个便显得像奇迹。

abstract.en: A word for a sum nobody can count to is also the word for a crowd nobody can count and a fortune nobody can spend.
abstract.cn: 一个谁也数不到的数目，同时也指谁也数不清的人群和谁也花不完的财产。

abstract.en: The same six zeros can mean a packed stadium or a private bank account, depending only on who is speaking.
abstract.cn: 同样的六个零，可以是满座的体育场，也可以是私人的银行账户，区别只在于说话的是谁。

abstract.en: Million is a measuring stick that people keep using to measure hope, so it never stays a pure number for long.
abstract.cn: million 是一把人们不断拿来量希望的尺子，所以它从不久久地停留为一个纯数字。
