senses.title: The item at position one million
senses.definition: the person or thing that comes at position one million in a long series, counted from the first
senses.definitionCN: 在一个很长的序列里，从第一个数起排在第一百万位的那个人或物
senses.example: The millionth copy rolled off the press just before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 第一百万份在黎明前下了印刷机。
senses.why: English builds ordinals with -th, the same ending that makes fourth and tenth, so millionth simply marks the place that follows the nine hundred ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-ninth item.
senses.whyCN: 英语用 -th 构成序数，和 fourth、tenth 用的是同一个词尾，所以 millionth 只是标出紧跟在九十九万九千九百九十九之后的那一位。

senses.title: One of a million equal parts
senses.definition: a fraction equal to one divided by a million, one piece of a whole cut into a million equal pieces
senses.definitionCN: 等于一除以一百万的分数，即把整体切成一百万等份后的一份
senses.example: The laser flashes once every millionth of a second.
senses.exampleCN: 激光每百万分之一秒闪一次。
senses.why: Latin had millesimus for a thousandth part, and English applies the same fraction logic one step higher: cut a whole into a million equal pieces, and any single piece is a millionth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本有 millesimus 表示千分之一，英语把同样的分数逻辑再往上推一级：把整体切成一百万等份，随便一份都是百万分之一。

senses.title: The millionth repetition, said in weariness
senses.definition: the millionth time something happens, used in speech to mean far too many repetitions rather than an exact count
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的第百万次，口语里用来指重复得没完没了，而不是精确计数
senses.example: For the millionth time, would you please close the door?
senses.exampleCN: 跟你说了多少回了，能不能把门关上？
senses.why: A million repetitions are past anyone's patience, so the phrase for the millionth time drifted from exact counting into a complaint about endless repetition.
senses.whyCN: 重复一百万次早已超过任何人的耐心，于是「第百万次」这个说法从精确计数滑成一句抱怨，指没完没了的重复。

intro.en: The ordinal is younger than the number it orders: Latin already had a word for a thousandth, but English millionth was built on the English noun with the ordinary ordinal ending.
intro.cn: 序数形式比它所排序的数更年轻：拉丁语早就有「千分之一」的词，而英语的 millionth 是拿英语名词加寻常的序数词尾造出来的。

items.en: Latin had mille for a thousand and millesimus for the thousandth, so the ordinal pattern behind millionth is older than the word itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语有 mille（千）和 millesimus（第一千），所以 millionth 背后的序数模式比这个词本身更老。

items.en: The base noun million was coined in Italian from mille plus the augmentative -one, naming a big thousand.
items.cn: 基数词 million 在意大利语里由 mille 加增大后缀 -one 造出，意为「大一号的千」。

items.en: French adopted million and used it in accounts and chronicles before English took it over.
items.cn: 法语收下 million，先在账目与编年史里使用，之后才被英语接过去。

items.en: English million named the exact number first, and the ordinal followed once people needed to point at a particular item in a series that long.
items.cn: 英语的 million 先指精确的数；等人们需要指出这么长的序列里的某一项时，序数形式才跟上。

items.en: Millionth was formed in English by adding -th to million on the model of fourth and tenth, and later spread into phrases of tired repetition.
items.cn: millionth 是在英语里照 fourth、tenth 的样子给 million 加 -th 造出的，后来又扩展到表示疲惫重复的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the forms built on the same million and the same ordinal ending; the near-meaning group gathers the fractions and position words that sit around it on the scale.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一个 million 与同一个序数词尾构成的词；近义组收在同一把尺子上围绕它的分数词与位置词。

entries.definition: Relating to a thousandth part, built on the Latin ordinal for a thousandth.

normalIntro.en: A Latin thousandth gave the model, the Italian big thousand gave the base, and English supplied the ordinary ordinal ending that turned it into a position and a fraction.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「千分之一」提供了样板，意大利语的「大一号的千」提供了基数，英语再添上寻常的序数词尾，把它变成位置与分数。

normal.en: Latin already had millesimus for the thousandth, so the shape of millionth was waiting long before million existed.
normal.cn: 拉丁语早有 millesimus 表示第一千，millionth 的骨架在 million 出现之前就已备好。

normal.en: Million was coined in Italian from mille and the suffix -one, which makes a word mean a larger version of its base.
normal.cn: million 是意大利语用 mille 加后缀 -one 造出的，那个后缀让词表示「基词的大一号」。

normal.en: English adds -th to million exactly as it adds it to four and ten, so the ordinal is ordinary building, not a new root.
normal.cn: 英语给 million 加 -th，和给 four、ten 加 -th 一模一样，是寻常构词，不是新词根。

normal.en: The plural millionths turns the ordinal into a countable fraction, one of a million equal slices.
normal.cn: 复数 millionths 把序数变成可数的分数，即一百万等份中的一份。

normal.en: For the millionth time is a phrase of impatience, because nobody can count that far and the number has become a way of saying again and again.
normal.cn: for the millionth time 是一句不耐烦的话，因为没人真能数到那里，这个数成了「一遍又一遍」的说法。

abstract.en: A museum counts every visitor, and the number that ends the counting is the one that gets the flowers.
abstract.cn: 博物馆数着每一位来客，而给数划上句号的那一位才会拿到花。

abstract.en: The same word can mean a prize position, a sliver of time, and a complaint about repetition, because all three are ways of being at the far end of a count.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以指一个获奖的位置、一小片时间、一句关于重复的抱怨，因为三者都是「数到尽头」的方式。

abstract.en: Being first is ordinary; being the millionth is only a story because somebody chose to keep counting.
abstract.cn: 成为第一个很平常；成为第一百万个之所以成故事，只因有人愿意一直数下去。

examples.en: The laser flashes once every millionth of a second.

examples.en: For the millionth time, she asked him to close the door.
examples.cn: 她不知道第多少回让他把门关上。

re-（再次）加 mind 的古老词干，义为「提醒；使想起」

senses.title: The thinking and feeling part of a person
senses.definition: the part of a person that thinks, feels, imagines and becomes aware of things
senses.definitionCN: 人身上用来思考、感受、想象并觉察事物的那部分
senses.example: A good question can open the mind instead of closing it.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好问题能打开人的头脑，而不是把它关上。
senses.why: Old English gemynd held memory and thought in one word, so the noun begins as the place where things are kept in awareness rather than as a plain synonym for the brain.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gemynd 把「记忆」和「思想」放在同一个词里，所以这个名词起初指「东西被留在觉察之中的那个地方」，而不是「大脑」的简单同义词。

senses.title: To look after or keep watch on
senses.definition: to take care of a person, place or thing, or to keep watch on it for a while
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人、某处或某物，或在一段时间内看住它
senses.example: Mind the baby while I answer the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我去开门，你照看一下孩子。
senses.why: If something is held in the mind, it is being watched; from that the verb grew the sense of looking after a person or a place, as when a neighbour minds the shop.
senses.whyCN: 某物既然被放在心里，就等于被看着；动词由此长出「照看某人或某处」的意思，比如邻居替你看着店。

senses.title: To be bothered by something
senses.definition: to be troubled or annoyed by something, or to object to it, especially in questions and negatives
senses.definitionCN: 因某事而不快或恼火，或对某事表示反对，多用于疑问句与否定句
senses.example: Do you mind if I open the window?
senses.exampleCN: 我把窗户打开，你介意吗？
senses.why: To mind something in the older idiom meant to be affected by it, so the modern question about objection is really asking whether the thing touches you at all.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的用法里，to mind 某件事意为「被它影响」，所以现代那句询问是否反对的话，其实是在问这件事碰不碰到你。

senses.title: Memory and recollection
senses.definition: a person's memory, or the act of bringing something back into awareness
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的记性，或把某事重新带回觉察之中的动作
senses.example: Her name has slipped my mind again.
senses.exampleCN: 我又把她的名字忘了。
senses.why: Because the noun first meant what is held in awareness, losing a name is described as its slipping out of the mind, and the word keeps that sense of a store that can be searched.
senses.whyCN: 因为名词最初指「被留在觉察里的东西」，名字想不起来就说它从心里滑了出去，这个词便保留了「一个可以翻找的储藏处」这层意思。

senses.title: Intention or settled opinion
senses.definition: a decision or intention that a person has settled on, especially one that can be changed
senses.definitionCN: 一个人定下来的决定或打算，尤指还可以更改的那种
senses.example: He changed his mind about the trip at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一刻改变了出行的主意。
senses.why: A decision is what a person settles in the mind, so making up or changing one's mind treats the mind as the place where a choice is fixed or revised.
senses.whyCN: 决定是人「在心里定下来」的东西，所以下决心或改主意，都把心当作一个把选择钉住或改写的场所。

intro.en: Mind is native English rather than borrowed: an old Germanic noun for memory and thought, related through a shared prehistoric root to the Latin word for the intellect.
intro.cn: mind 是英语本族词而非借词：一个表示记忆与思想的古老日耳曼名词，通过共同的史前词根与拉丁语表示「理智」的词相连。

items.en: A reconstructed root for thinking is generally placed behind both the Latin and the Germanic words, though the exact path is inferred rather than recorded.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构的「思考」词根同时位于拉丁语与日耳曼语这两组词之后，具体路径是推断出来的，并非有记录可查。

items.en: Latin mens meant mind or intellect and grew from that same root, which is why mental and mind are distant cousins rather than strangers.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mens 意为心智、理智，出自同一个词根，所以 mental 与 mind 是远亲，而不是陌生人。

items.en: Germanic speakers formed a noun for memory and thought from the root; the reconstructed form is generally written with an old prefix ga-.
items.cn: 日耳曼语使用者由这个词根造出表示记忆与思想的名词，一般认为它带有一个古老的前缀 ga-，写作重构形式。

items.en: Old English gemynd covered memory, thought and the seat of both, and the ge- prefix later dropped away.
items.cn: 古英语 gemynd 兼指记忆、思想以及承载二者的所在，前缀 ge- 后来脱落。

items.en: Modern English mind keeps the noun senses of thought, memory and intention and adds verb senses of caring, watching and objecting.
items.cn: 现代英语的 mind 保留思想、记忆、意向等名词义，又添上照看、留心、反对等动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the English words built on the same mind; the near-meaning group gathers the body part, the faculty, the focus and the settled view that people confuse with it.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个 mind 上的英语词；近义组收容易被它混淆的身体器官、心智能力、注意力与定见。

entries.definition: Full of mind in the sense of paying attention, alert and considerate.
entries.definitionCN: 在「留心」的意义上充满 mind，即警觉而体贴的。

entries.definition: Without mind, meaning done with no thought or care behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 没有 mind，指做事不带思考或不在意。

entries.definition: A settled way of thinking, a mind set in a particular position.
entries.definitionCN: 固定下来的思维方式，把心思摆在一个特定位置上。

entries.definition: To put something back into someone's mind, built with the prefix re-.
entries.definitionCN: 用前缀 re- 构成，把某事重新放回某人的心里。

entries.definition: The physical organ inside the skull, a body part rather than the thinking self.
entries.definitionCN: 颅骨里的实体器官，是身体的一部分，而不是思考的主体。

entries.definition: The faculty that stores and brings back what was known.
entries.definitionCN: 储存并唤回已知之事的那个能力。

entries.definition: The act of holding mental focus on one thing at a time.
entries.definitionCN: 一次把心思集中在一件事上的动作。

entries.definition: A view a person holds, whether or not it has been settled into a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人所持的看法，无论是否已成为决定。

normalIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, and its family keeps returning to what is held in awareness, whether that is a memory, a watch kept on something, or a view that can be changed.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼本族词，同族词反复回到「被留在觉察里的东西」——无论那是一段记忆、对某物的看守，还是一个可以更改的看法。

normal.en: Old English gemynd meant memory before it meant thought, which is why keep in mind sounds like storing something rather than reasoning about it.
normal.cn: 古英语 gemynd 先指记忆，后指思想，所以 keep in mind 听起来更像把东西存起来，而不是对它推理。

normal.en: Latin mens and English mind come from the same old root, so mental is a relative and not a borrowed stranger.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mens 与英语 mind 出自同一个古老词根，所以 mental 是亲戚，不是借来的陌生人。

normal.en: Mindful adds -ful, full of mind, and describes someone whose attention is fully present in the room.
normal.cn: mindful 加 -ful，意为「充满 mind」，形容一个人的注意力完全在场。

normal.en: Mindless adds -less, without mind, and describes action done with no thought behind it.
normal.cn: mindless 加 -less，意为「没有 mind」，形容做事背后不带思考。

normal.en: The verb mind began as keeping something in the mind, then split into watching over it and being troubled by it.
normal.cn: 动词 mind 从「把某物留在心里」出发，随后分成「看住它」与「被它困扰」两条路。

abstract.en: A word that begins as memory and ends as objection shows how much of thinking is really about what we cannot put down.
abstract.cn: 一个从记忆出发、到介意收尾的词，说明思考里有很大一部分其实是关于放不下的东西。

abstract.en: To mind a child and to mind the noise are the same verb, because care and irritation both begin with attention.
abstract.cn: 照看孩子与介意噪音是同一个动词，因为关心和恼火都从注意力开始。

abstract.en: Changing one's mind is not a failure of the word but its oldest freedom, a place where a choice can still be moved.
abstract.cn: 改主意不是这个词的失灵，而是它最老的自由——那个选择仍可被挪动的地方。

examples.en: The news opened her mind to a side of the story she had never considered.
examples.cn: 这条新闻让她看到了故事里从未想过的一面。

examples.en: Mind the baby while I answer the door.
examples.cn: 我去开门，你照看一下孩子。

examples.en: He changed his mind about the trip at the last minute.
examples.cn: 他在最后一刻改变了出行的主意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埋的」——把心事埋在心底；mind 既是头脑，也是介意与照看。

root: 古英语 gemynd（记忆、思想），源于日耳曼语中带前缀 ga- 的「思考」名词，与拉丁语 mens（心智）同出一个重构的史前词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the inner place where things are kept in awareness; from it come memory, attention, intention, and the verb senses of watching over something and being troubled by it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「东西被留在觉察之中的内心之处」；记忆、注意力、意向，以及「看住某物」与「被某物困扰」这两个动词义，都从这里分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person alone under a dim lamp, fingers pressed to the temple, every sound shut outside the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人独自坐在昏黄的灯下，手指按着太阳穴，所有声音都关在门外。

branches.en: a room lit by one lamp where all sound stops at the door
branches.cn: 一盏灯照着的房间，所有声音都停在门外

branches.en: a name that will not come back however hard one searches
branches.cn: 怎么翻找也想不起来的一个名字

branches.en: a neighbour watching the counter for an hour
branches.cn: 邻居替他看一小时柜台

branches.en: a question that makes a person pause before answering
branches.cn: 一个让人停顿一下才回答的问题

branches.en: a decision rewritten in the last minute
branches.cn: 最后一刻被改写的决定

intro.en: The word stands on an Old English noun of memory, an old Germanic prefix that fell away, a Latin cousin for the intellect, and English endings that build attention and the lack of it.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语表示记忆的名词、一个后来脱落的老日耳曼前缀、一个指理智的拉丁语亲戚，以及构成「留心」与「不留心」的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies a close cousin rather than a parent: mens names the intellect from the same prehistoric thinking root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供的是近亲而不是父辈：mens 出自同一个史前「思考」词根，指理智。
